> **Stamped:** 2026-08-27 at `57c34d8`+HS.1 (**ad-hoc, user-directed — not a lane task, no plan file. The masterplan stays closed at 157/157.** **The Harvest tab grew a second engine: the HAND SWEEP.** Same reader as the auto harvest — `harvestPosts`/`harvestReplies` verbatim, so a swept row IS a harvested row — but driven by the reader's own scrolling instead of by `runHarvest`'s scroll robot, with an on-page HUD in the bottom-left dock carrying the row count and how far back the sweep has reached. **Extension-only: not one server file changed**, because the wire it needed already existed (`POST /harvest/runs` + `/harvest/rows`, scope `'all'`). Five things a later session needs. **(1) The two keys have one writer each** — `harvest:handSweep` is the ARM (panel writes, either side removes) and `harvest:handSweep:stats` is the PROGRESS (content script writes, panel reads); the stats blob carries the session's `startedAt`, so a previous sweep's numbers can never render as this one's. **(2) The mode comes from the PAGE, never from the mode tabs** — `handSweepTargetFor(url)` is built on `isAtTarget`, the same function the capture gate uses, so the button's enable check and the page's gate cannot disagree; `/media`, `/highlights`, `/following` and a status page are all un-sweepable. **(3) A failed flush RETRIES and never drops** — the deliberate opposite of the HV.2 passive tap (a lost sighting is a missing point on a view curve; a lost sweep row is an action the user watched a counter for). Back-off 15 s, stop drains ≤10 batches. **(4) The capture pass is throttled to 400 ms with a trailing pass** — it reads every article in the DOM and content.ts's `scan` fires per animation frame; without the throttle a sweep would cost ~14k DOM queries a second while scrolling. **(5) The bottom-left corner is a DOCK now** (`.stratus-dock`), not two elements that each positioned themselves — the radar sweep chip is order 1, the HUD order 2. Any future persistent overlay joins it rather than picking its own 16px. **Browser end-to-end is OWED**: the gates are green (2615 tests / 133 files, typecheck, lint, extension build) but nothing here has been driven against a live x.com profile — the HUD's paint, the throttle's feel and the SPA-navigation pause are all convention-tested only, like every other `content.ts` surface.)

> pre-computed answer to "where does X live and how is it wired".
> **Maintenance rule:** any commit that adds/moves/deletes a file, route, table,
> worker, extension surface, or pattern MUST update the touched section here (and
> re-stamp the header). Every plan produced by `/plan-feature` ends with a
> docs-sync task that includes this file.

## 1. Thirty-second orientation

Single-user service (one human, one bearer token) with four goals and a **hard
scope ceiling** (a feature not serving one of these does not get built):

1. Schedule X posts a week ahead (calendar + 60s publisher worker).
2. Track metrics over time on published posts — **$0 DOM harvest only since 2026-08-12 (XD.1)**; the paid 03:00 UTC snapshot pass is deleted and the snapshot tables are frozen history.
3. Voice library — stash other people's tweets via $0 DOM scrape for style analysis.
4. Circles — the people layer: CRM stages, conversations/open loops, relationship-aware drafting, Playbook, warmth (quests/digest/icebreakers).

Runtime: **Bun ≥1.1 + Hono** server on Hetzner (`https://stratus-narcis.duckdns.org`, systemd `stratus.service`, deployed via `scripts/deploy.sh`) + **Chrome MV3 side-panel extension** (Vite + React, loaded unpacked). State: **local SQLite via `bun:sqlite`** + Drizzle (`sqlite-core`), auto-migrated at boot. AI: xAI Grok via `src/grok/` (text `askGrok`, images `generateImages`). No queue, no Redis — one in-process `setInterval` worker (the publisher; it is also the only thing in the repo that spends X-API money, via `createPost`).

## 2. Root directory

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE.md` | Session guardrails ONLY (slimmed 2026-07-23): invariants, workflow pointers, stack quirks, cost sheet. Update only when a guardrail changes. |
| `docs/PHASE-HISTORY.md` | Full chronological phase ledger (moved verbatim out of CLAUDE.md 2026-07-23). **Docs-sync tasks append their phase entry here, not in CLAUDE.md.** |
| `PLAN.md` | **Canonical build plan, goals 1–3** (cadence ladders, phased build). |
| `CIRCLES-PLAN.md` | **Canonical build plan, goal 4** (phases C0–C10, all shipped; C10 = the notifications surface, planned separately in `plans/2026-07-16-notifications.md` and folded in at NT.7). |
| `SURFACES-PLAN.md` | Canonical plan for the S-phases (S0.x patches, S1 explorer, S2 MCP, S3 studio, S4 images). |
| `X-API-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md` | Reference-only X API spec: endpoint semantics, pricing, policy quirks. Never a build plan. |
| `X-API-PRICING-REFERENCE.md` | Raw pricing tables. |

RS.3 moved queue admission onto the sweep filters and RS.7 hid the thresholds; this removed the leftover second opinion outright. **`src/shared/radarSweep.ts::passesSweep` is now the ONE rule that decides what a tweet qualifies for, and the Radar's sweep gear is the only place it is tuned — do not reintroduce a classifier here.** The file keeps its NAME (shim + docs churn is not worth it); its header says all of this. |

| `src/shared/cannon.ts` | **CQ.1 (NEW)** — the arbitrage reading of a sighting, `replyBand.ts`'s twin down to the header-comment discipline. Dependency-free by contract (its ONLY import is `type TweetSignals` from `./replyBand.ts`, erased under `verbatimModuleSyntax`), so it inlines into the content IIFE (§7.26) through the shim `extension/src/cannon.ts` (§7.27) and the page and the server can never disagree on what "worth arbitraging" means. Surface: `CannonThresholds {scoreMin, maxAgeMin, redAgeMin, placedTarget}`, `CANNON` (the shipped defaults, which **ARE** the `cannon` registry group's defaults — UI.7, asserted by a group-shape test), `cannonScore(s) = views / (replies + 1)`, `isCannonEligible(s, t=CANNON)` (`ageMin <= maxAgeMin && score >= scoreMin` — it deliberately does NOT know about roster membership; that half needs the people layer and would break the IIFE contract), `cannonAgeTone(ageMin, t)` (strict `>`, so exactly `redAgeMin` still reads `'ok'`). The `+ 1` is the zero guard **and** the source measurement's own formula — not `max(replies, 1)`; changing it silently rescales every stored score. **The header carries the §7.33 corpus replay and its verdict**, which is the reusable half: the borrowed 5,000 floor was replayed over our own `harvest_rows` (`mode IN ('timeline','posts')`, 30 days — 1,841 rows / 296 handles / 1,650 distinct tweets: p50 45.3 · p75 65.8 · p90 **120.5** · p95 270.0 · p99 3977.3) and **cleared by only 0.60% of rows**, i.e. under the ~2% bar, so it was REFUSED and the shipped `scoreMin` is the measured p90 rounded to **120**. Two caveats a recalibration starts from are recorded there too: harvest rows are captured at arbitrary post ages while the queue only scores posts under `maxAgeMin`, and the same corpus scored the ROSTER way runs p50 33.8 / p90 100.2 — the roster floor and the per-sighting floor are one knob today, and diverging distributions want splitting rather than a compromise. Consumers: `settings/cannonThresholds.ts`, `routes/cannon.ts` (the `belowFloor` floor), `extension/src/shared/radar.ts::cannonQueue`, `serverSettings.ts`. **RS.3 removed the page-side consumer:** `isCannonEligible`'s score half stopped being a capture rule (`src/shared/radarSweep.ts` owns admission now) and survives only as `cannonQueue`'s read-time DISPLAY rule, so `content.ts` no longer imports this module or reads `x.cannon.*` at all — the camped-roster arm takes its age bound from `x.sweep.maxAgeMin`. Do not re-add a cannon read to the page without deciding which of the two age rules wins. |
| `src/shared/radarSweep.ts` | **RS.1 (NEW)** — the admission rule for the Radar queue, `cannon.ts`'s sibling and the same discipline: **not one import, type or value** (so it inlines into the content IIFE, §7.26, through the shim `extension/src/radarSweep.ts`) and it reads **no store** — the config arrives as an ARGUMENT on both sides. Surface: `SweepConfig` (**13 fields since SW.1**), `SweepMediaFilter = 'any'\|'with'\|'without'`, `SWEEP` (the shipped defaults, which **ARE** the `sweep` registry group's defaults — a group-shape test asserts the group is exactly `keyof SweepConfig`), `SweepCandidate {views, likes, replies, ageMin, verified: boolean\|null, hasMedia: boolean\|null, promoted: boolean}`, `passesSweep(c, cfg = SWEEP)`, **`passesContentGates(c, cfg)`** (SW.1 — the ads + media half, exported because it is NOT a metric gate: the camped/circle bypass arms call it directly, the reach `maxAgeMin` already had), `sweepNeedsVerified(cfg)` / **`sweepNeedsMedia(cfg)` / `sweepNeedsPromoted(cfg)`** (the same named-skip perf contract, one per DOM read; the media read ships SKIPPED because the gate ships `'any'`), **`RADAR_QUEUE_TTL_MS = 24h` (RQ.3 — how long a sighting stays queueable; moved here from `extension/src/shared/radar.ts`, which now re-exports it as `RADAR_TTL_MS` so no call site moved, because `GET /radar/sightings?queue=true` rebuilds the panel's queue and the server's window and the page's `pruneStale` must be one number)**, and the session half: `SWEEP_STATE_KEY = 'radar:sweep'`, `SweepSession {startedAt, expiresAt}` (ISO), `startSweepSession(nowMs, cfg)`, `sweepActiveAt(raw, nowMs)`, `sweepMinutesLeft(session, nowMs)` (RS.4). **Three contracts a change here must not break.** (a) **Gate ORDER is a perf contract** (§7.4 applied to a DOM read): `applyBand` re-runs on every mutation burst, so the six numeric comparisons — already in hand from the one aria parse — decide first, and the caller pays for `readVerified` only when `sweepNeedsVerified(cfg)`; that helper is one line and is deliberately NOT inlined, because the skip is only reviewable if it has a name. (b) **`0` on a `max*` means "no ceiling" and is the module's only sentinel** — `maxAgeMin` is the exception, always enforced on every arm including both bypasses, registry floor 1, and its `0` is an out-of-range value rather than "unlimited". (c) **`verified: null` under `verifiedOnly` FAILS** — the deliberate inversion of §7.11, because this is a gate, not a bucket; **`hasMedia: null` fails under BOTH `'with'` and `'without'` for the same reason (SW.1)**, with the asymmetry stated in the module: the page's reader answers `false` (never `null`) when its selectors drift, so a drift empties the queue under `'with'` and silently admits media under `'without'`. `sweepActiveAt` is lenient like `readServerConfig` (anything that isn't `{startedAt, expiresAt}` with a parseable FUTURE expiry returns `null` = manual, never throws) and **is what makes expiry read-time rather than timer-owned**; exactly `expiresAt` is already over. `sweepMinutesLeft` rounds **up** and floors at 0, and takes a RESOLVED session so a label can never be what decides whether a sweep is live. The header carries every default's provenance: `minViews: 300` and `maxReplies: 40` are **restated from `BAND`, never imported** (§7.33) so the sweep can be tuned without moving the classifier that draws the border. **RS.8 moved three of them** (user-directed): `maxViews 0 → 2000`, `maxLikes 0 → 20`, `verifiedOnly false → true`. Two consequences a later reader needs: (i) the shipped set is now a **band**, not a half-open range — a `0` on a `max*` is still "no ceiling", it is simply no longer what ships; (ii) **`sweepNeedsVerified(SWEEP)` is now `true`**, so the gate-order perf skip in (a) no longer fires by default and the capture arm pays for `readVerified` on every candidate that clears the numbers. If the queue ever goes silently empty, `verifiedOnly` is the FIRST switch to flip — an unreadable author counts as not verified, so a badge-selector drift and a correctly-empty feed look identical from the panel. Consumers: `settings/registry.ts` (defaults), `extension/src/shared/serverSettings.ts::readSweep`, `content.ts` (the capture arm + the chip), `sidepanel/Radar.tsx` (Start/Stop + the countdown). |
| `src/shared/language.ts` | **ML.1 (NEW)** — the language profile table + script detection, `replyBand.ts`/`cannon.ts`'s third sibling and the same discipline: **ZERO runtime imports** (a value import breaks the IIFE, §7.26), reached from the page through the shim `extension/src/language.ts` (§7.27), and it reads **no settings store** — the profile table is CODE, not a knob (`bandThresholds` deliberately does not apply: "Arabic is weight 1" is a fact about X's counter, not a number to recalibrate). Surface: `LanguageProfile {code, name, aliases, script, rtl, maxChars, registerAxis}`, `LANGUAGE_PROFILES` (11: ja zh ko ar he ru es pt fr de ro), `MAX_WEIGHTED = 280`, `weightedLength`, `detectScript`, `resolveLanguageProfile`. **`weightedLength` is twitter-text's rule verbatim, over CODEPOINTS** (`for (const ch of text)` — `String.length` counts UTF-16 units and double-counts astral codepoints; that WAS `Replies.tsx`'s counter): weight 1 for `[0,4351]`, `[8192,8205]`, `[8208,8223]`, `[8242,8247]`, weight 2 otherwise. **The counter-intuitive consequence is in the header and is the reason there is a table rather than a Japanese special case: Arabic, Cyrillic, Hebrew and Devanagari sit inside `[0,4351]` ⇒ weight 1, i.e. the FULL 280 with no length change; CJK/Kana/Hangul ⇒ weight 2, i.e. ~140.** `maxChars` per profile is that budget in the language's own characters — never derive it from "is it English". `detectScript` votes over **letters only** (`\p{L}`; digits/whitespace/punctuation/emoji cast no vote, so a Japanese post quoting "Claude Code" still reads `ja`) and carries the two ambiguity rules explicitly: **kana ⇒ `ja` (Han votes fold into Japanese the moment any kana appears), Han alone ⇒ `zh`, Hangul ⇒ `ko`**; `'latin'`-script profiles are resolvable by NAME but never detected (the script cannot pick between es/pt/fr/de/ro), and `null` = UNKNOWN (§7.11 — nothing voted, no simple majority, or a tie), never "English". `resolveLanguageProfile` matches case/space-insensitively over code+name+aliases and returns `null` on a near-miss rather than guessing. `registerAxis` names that language's OWN politeness axis in one sentence (だ・である/です・ます/敬語, MSA vs dialect, 해체/해요체/합니다체, T–V) — a per-language axis, deliberately not a second persona. Consumers: `src/x/replies/language.ts`, `src/x/replies/prompt.ts` (`renderLanguageClause`), `extension/src/sidepanel/Replies.tsx` (the counter). |

Zero-dep + IIFE-safe, config arrives as an ARGUMENT, the module reads no store. **`engine.ts` re-exports every public name** — no caller migrated its import path (HM decision 6: the byte-untouched RL.1 suite IS the proof the move changed nothing). Shim `extension/src/humanize.ts` (§5). |
| `src/shared/postCoach.ts` | **SC.1** — deterministic pre-publish coach: `scoreDraft(text, {lexicon?, isReply?}) → {score 0–100, band top/ship/almost/rework, checks, counts}`. 29 pure rules over facts computed once (hygiene 13 / craft 7 / signal 9 — incl. the 15-raw-line show-more `fix` and the $0.20 URL-surcharge line, which SURFACES invariant #1 while `calendar.ts`'s 400 stays the only gate). Score = min(mean pass1/nudge0.5/fix0 over hygiene+craft ×100, 40+60×signal passRate), capped 25 under 4 words/15 chars and 65 under 7 words/30 chars (x-builder §L2 arithmetic ported as-is; everything else re-implemented — upstream has no LICENSE). `isReply: true` skips `hook_opener`+`breathing_room` and passes `url_cost`. `DEFAULT_LEXICON` is deliberately EMPTY (decision 7; the lexicon is an ARGUMENT, the module reads no store) — **SC.7 fills it** from `GET /x/coach/lexicon` (`routes/coach.ts`), and it moves exactly two rules: `concrete_detail` (specificTerms, via `hasAnchor`) and `hook_opener`'s vocative branch (tribeTerms, post-only). Zero-dep + IIFE-safe; the extension re-export shim arrives with SC.3. Exports `COACH_DISCLAIMER`/`COACH_BAND_LABEL` so every consumer renders the same floor-not-target copy (decision 4: no surface sorts, gates, or refuses on the score). Consumers: the Composer column (SC.3), the **server** (`buildCoachScoreEffectiveness`, SC.5 — the only non-panel caller; originals are graded with the POST rules, i.e. default `isReply:false`) and, through `sidepanel/CoachChip.tsx`, the four reply-variant pickers (**SC.4** — `isReply: true` there, so `hook_opener`+`breathing_room` are skipped and a reply grades over **27** checks, not 29; nothing hardcodes either number). |
| `src/shared/postFormat.ts` | **SC.2** — deterministic post-format classifier: `classifyFormat(text) → PostFormat` (14 formats: would_you_rather, poll_list, binary_choice, hot_take, confession, milestone, audience_cta, question, data_comparison, story, list, one_liner, substance, other) + `FORMAT_LABELS` + `POST_FORMATS` (declared in cascade order). **Format = the FOURTH orthogonal axis** (pillar = topic, register = tone, angle = reply stance, format = structure); the label is measurement metadata (§7.19), NEVER stored (SC decision 2 — classified at read time from `posts_published.text`/`scheduled_posts.text` so a fix retroactively re-labels history). Ordered cascade, earlier wins: declared shapes → frame openers (hot_take/confession/milestone) → CTA markers → question → data → story → structural fallbacks; `substance` = multi-line matched-nothing, `one_liner` = single-line matched-nothing, `other` = only degenerate text (RT/URL-only/<4 words — §7.11). Normalizes X's stored HTML entities + curly quotes and strips t.co URLs first. Fixtures are hand-labelled REAL `posts_published` rows; measured distribution over 136 originals: substance 43% / cta 15% / list 13% / story 13% / **other 0.7%** (plan bar: <35%). Zero-dep + IIFE-safe; **the shim landed at SC.5** (`extension/src/postFormat.ts`, §5). Consumed by the server's `buildFormatEffectiveness` (SC.5), `src/shared/postCooldown.ts` (SC.6) and — since SC.6 — the Composer itself (`classifyFormat(coachInput)` matches the draft against the cooldown cells). |
| `src/shared/postCooldown.ts` | **SC.6 (NEW)** — format cooldown: `buildCooldowns(posts: {text, postedAt}[], now, windowDays = 7) → CooldownCell[]` (`{format, count, status clear/warming/cooldown, exempt, lastPostedAt ISO, exampleText}`), one cell per format present in the window, in `POST_FORMATS` cascade order. `COOLDOWN_THRESHOLD = 4` / `WARMING_THRESHOLD = 2` / `COOLDOWN_WINDOW_DAYS = 7`. **`COOLDOWN_EXEMPT_FORMATS = ['substance','one_liner','other']`** — the three fallback labels mean "no format detected", so their cells ship with `exempt: true` and a pinned `clear` status (D146(b)'s resolution; at 43% `substance` a counted fallback would be a permanent chip). **The x-builder Jaccard idea-clustering is deliberately NOT ported** — measured over the real 137-original corpus, the most similar same-format pair inside any 7-day window scores 0.238 (p95 0.077) against a 0.45 threshold, so it would be silent forever; idea-repetition already has an owner in `monitor.ts`'s `nearDuplicate` (shingle Jaccard ≥0.8 / 14d). Zero-dep + IIFE-safe; **no extension shim** (the panel reads cells off the route and mirrors the wire shape in `shared/types.ts`). Consumers: `GET /x/posts/cooldowns` (`routes/calendar.ts`). |

Zero-dep + IIFE-safe, `replyBand.ts`/`cannon.ts`/`radarSweep.ts`/`language.ts`'s next sibling; the shim `extension/src/searchQuery.ts` lands at **OU.5** (§7.27), so until then this module has **no consumer at all** and the suite is its only caller. Surface: `SearchQuery` (19 fields, the cheatsheet-complete set), `Problem {level 'error'|'warn', field, message}` / `CompileResult {query,length,overLimit,problems}`, `MAX_QUERY_LENGTH` **512** / `MAX_TERMS_PER_FIELD` 20 / `MAX_TERM_LENGTH` 120 (the last two exported so the route and the form can explain a silent drop), `SEARCH_LANGS` (16 codes — an **allowlist, not a regex**, because an unknown `lang:` returns ZERO results on X, which reads exactly like "no matches"), `FAVES_LADDER` [50…5000] + `nextRung`/`prevRung`, `parseSearchQuery` (normalizing validator, `null` ONLY on a non-object — `parseHumanizerConfig`'s shape), `compileSearchQuery`, `searchUrl(q, opts?)`. **Web dialect only, and that IS the cost decision** — invariant #8's opposite made on the record: X API v2 has no `min_faves`/`min_retweets`/`min_replies` at any tier, so the API version would pay ~$0.005 per returned result to discard most of them. Do NOT add a `dialect` param, an `api` compile path, or a threshold estimator (decision 10). **The split that makes the rest legible: `parseSearchQuery` owns SHAPE, `compileSearchQuery` owns CONTENT.** A bad handle survives normalization and returns as a per-field `Problem` instead of vanishing between what the user typed and what the preview shows — which is also what lets a stored row skip re-validation while the compile still reports faults. Rules the module owns: the `any` group is **always parenthesized, even at one member** (AND binds tighter than OR on X, so a later clause must never be able to re-associate it) and `OR` is uppercase (lowercase is a literal word); a `"` in ANY term is an **error, never a strip** (X has no escape character); floors are positive ints and `0` means absent (a deliberate §7.11 carve-out — here `0` is a real intent, and `min_faves:0` is inert noise eating the 512 budget); `replies`/`media` are enums because two booleans could say exclude-and-only at once, while `hasLinks` gets both arms because a boolean cannot contradict itself and `noRetweets` gets only the negative one; dates must be real calendar dates (`2026-02-31` errors, `2026-7-1` errors) and `until < since` errors; **a query with no MATCHER — only floors/filters/negations — errors**, because that is a request for the firehose minus a bit of it. **Never throws** (every field re-guarded despite being typed, since the input crosses a wire) and an invalid clause is SKIPPED from the best-effort string rather than emitted into it. `searchUrl` returns `null` iff any problem is `error`, so the type system carries the refuse-before-run gate; `f=live` unless the effective sort (`opts.sort ?? q.sort ?? 'live'`) says `top`. **An unrecognized `sort` DROPS rather than falling back** — that one default lives outside the module (the `x.outliers.sort` knob, `top`), and freezing `'live'` in here would let the column default stand in for the product default (D200). **The header comment carries the 2026-08-24 live x.com operator spot check** (§7.33 — X's parser is the oracle and it lives off-machine; a retired operator returns the UNFILTERED firehose, which looks identical to a working feature), naming what each check proved. Re-run it before trusting a new operator, and DELETE a retired one rather than leaving it compiling. |
| `src/shared/xRanker.ts` | **XR.1 (NEW)** — X's published For You ranking weights + the `ranking_scorer.rs` arithmetic. `searchQuery.ts`/`language.ts`'s next zero-dep sibling and the same contract: **not one import**, so it inlines into the content IIFE (§7.26) at XR.7; the shims landed at **XR.5** (`extension/src/xRanker.ts`), so the panel now compiles it in; the content IIFE is still XR.7's. Surface: `XHeadName` + `X_HEADS` (**26 heads**, each `{weight, param, provenance, label, observable, continuous?, note?}`), `POSITIVE_SUM_MEMBERS` (18) / `NEGATIVE_SUM_MEMBERS` (5) / `X_WEIGHT_SUMS` `{positive 43.34, negative 367.22, total 410.56}`, `NEGATIVE_SCORES_OFFSET` 0.001, `BIDIRECTIONAL_FOLLOW_REPLY_BOOST` 15.0, `OON_WEIGHT_FACTOR` 0.75, `AUTHOR_DIVERSITY {decay .5, floor .25}`, `offsetScore` / `scoreHeads` / `replyWeightFor` / `oonApplies` / `diversityMultiplier` / `normalizeScore`. **FACTS ONLY — the estimator is `xRankerSignals.ts` (XR.2), a separate file precisely so the two can never be confused.** Transcribed 2026-09-02 **directly from `xai-org/x-algorithm` @ `7ba77684`** (`params/param.rs`, `params/config.rs:40`, `scorers/ranking_scorer.rs`), Apache-2.0, attribution in the header — **not from Bangermeter, whose copy the plan named at a `~/Downloads` path that no longer exists** (D225). Four ported traps, each with a why-comment: **(1)** `positive_sum` EXCLUDES the three `cont_*` heads and both bidirectional boosts — it only shows on the negative branch, so getting it wrong is invisible to a test that scores good posts; **(2)** terms split by the sign of the **term**, not of the weight; **(3)** `offsetScore` **squashes** a net-negative into `[0, 0.000894437)` rather than clamping, so negative posts keep their relative order — the `raw > 0` guard belongs in `normalizeScore`, the display boundary; **(4)** `oonApplies` is a boolean GATE (0.75 lands once, never squared) and fires for in-network replies/reposts too, because `EnableOonRescoreForInNetworkRepliesRetweets` defaults **true**. A head with no probability is **skipped**, never `0` (§7.11) — absent from `contributions` and from both sums. `normalizeScore` is **the one function here that is ours**: parameter-free `100*raw/(raw+baseline)`, baseline lands on exactly 50, bounded (0,100) so a viral outlier cannot run the scale away. **No settings knob for any of it — a published weight is a transcribed fact, not a tunable**, and X syncs these from production, so re-verification against a newer commit is a real (cheap) future task. |
| `src/shared/xRankerSignals.ts` | **XR.2 (NEW)** — the ESTIMATOR half of the ranker port; `xRanker.ts` holds facts, this holds guesses, and the split is why there are two files. **The one sibling allowed imports:** value + type from `./xRanker.ts`, `./postCoach.ts`, `./postFormat.ts` — `postCooldown.ts` is the precedent (it value-imports `postFormat`), and all four inline together into the content IIFE at XR.7, so §7.26 still holds. Surface: `X_BASELINE_P` (20 signal-free priors, `provenance: 'bangermeter-estimate'` — deliberately NOT the measured median, plan Decision 4), `X_OBSERVED_RATES` + `X_OBSERVED_RATES_SAMPLE` (**XR.3: measured, `provenance: 'measured'`, n=766 off `harvest_rows mode='timeline'`, 2026-07-24..2026-08-17 — favorite `0.029412`, reply `0.019774`, retweet **`0`**, because 66% of our feed posts have no reposts and zero IS the median; the head goes one-sided and nothing divides by it**), `ENGAGEMENT_SHRINKAGE_PSEUDO_VIEWS` 2000 (**XR.4 measured and KEPT it**: beta-binomial MoM ~1066 on `favorite`, NO between-post signal on `reply`/`retweet`, and even K=500 leaves 1.9% of sightings above the old 65 — E's narrow span is a 297-median-view corpus, not the smoother), `MIN_VIDEO_DURATION_MS` 10_000, `DraftFeatures`, `ModifierSource`/`RankerModifier`/**`X_MODIFIERS` (23 entries)**, `RankerBand` + **`RANKER_BAND_CUTS` (XR.4: two MEASURED pairs, `draft {typical 56, strong 68}` off 308 own published originals and `measured {typical 46, strong 51}` off 3,567 harvested sightings — each the q1/q3 of the corpus its scale is applied to, so a band means a QUARTILE POSITION; `provenance: 'measured'` + `RANKER_BAND_CUTS_SAMPLE`)** + **`rankerDraftBand`/`rankerMeasuredBand` (two functions, never `rankerBand(score, scale)` — `latestOwnReplyRows`'s no-flag rule: an E score of 61 reads `typical` on its own cuts and `strong` on the draft ones, silently)**, `RANKER_BAND_LABEL`, `RANKER_DISCLAIMER`, `signalsToHeadPs`, **`scoreDraftRanker` (C)**, **`scoreMeasured` (E)**, `vqvEligible`, `signalFreeBaselineRaw`, `positiveFloorRaw`, `SIGNAL_FREE_SCORE` 50, `resetRankerBaselineCache`. **Every `X_MODIFIERS` entry names a source in OUR vocabulary** — `{kind:'coach', id, on:'pass'|'flag'}` (18), `{kind:'format', format}` (4), `{kind:'feature', flag}` (1) — asserted against the LIVE `postCoach` check list, so renaming a check breaks the suite instead of silently disabling a modifier. Bangermeter's `contentModifiers` are **not** ported (Decision 1); the suite asserts their ten ids are absent. Four things a later task must not 'clean up': **(1)** a modifier multiplies a PROBABILITY and is clamped at the head ceiling (`cont_dwell_time` 600s, everything else 1); **(2)** `open_link` is a REACH fact — the ranker PAYS 0.2 for a link — and invariant #1's $0.20 surcharge is an API BILLING rule, so `url_cost` is deliberately absent from the table; **(3)** network position is KNOWN for a draft (`inNetwork: true`, flipped by `assumeOutOfNetwork`) and UNKNOWN for a sighting, which is why `oonApplies` maps unknown to `false`; **(4)** `vqv` is weighted 0.0, so its strict >10s gate documents rather than scores — an unknown duration (a GIF) earns nothing, stricter than Bangermeter, per §7.11. Both baselines are DERIVED from the prior tables and memoized, never written down (the `X_WEIGHT_SUMS` rule). |

| `grok/pricing.ts` | Token + per-image price maps (`priceForImage`). |
| `grok/routes/ask.ts` | `POST /grok/ask` passthrough. |
| `grok/index.ts` | `mountGrok` (refuses to mount without `XAI_API_KEY`). |
| `openrouter/client.ts` | **AI.1** — `askOpenRouter`, the ONE place all OpenRouter calls go (a second LLM provider, sibling to grok). `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` (OpenAI shape), structured outputs via `response_format.json_schema` (NOT xAI's `text.format`), `usage:{include:true}` + `provider:{require_parameters:true}` ALWAYS; **cost comes straight off `usage.cost` (USD) — NO price table** (warns on a 2xx with tokens but no cost, §9.1); retry/auth/logCost mirror askGrok; `cost_events` platform `'openrouter'`; soft `OPENROUTER_DAILY_BUDGET_USD` watchdog (default $1.00, log-only). `DEFAULT_MODEL='anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5'` (AI.2 settings own the real default); optional `fetchImpl` test seam; NO `promptCacheKey` (no OpenAI-compat field). INERT until AI.2 wires `askLLM`/`/llm` routes. |

| `llm/ask.ts` | **AI.2** — `askLLM(opts, {defaults})`, the provider dispatcher (§7.1 extended: the ONE place picking grok vs openrouter; each provider keeps its own single entry point). Resolution `opts.provider ?? settings.provider`; merge precedence **opts > DB AI settings > call-site defaults** encoded once here (temperature/maxOutputTokens/reasoningEffort; model: openrouter→`opts.model ?? settings.openrouterModel`, grok→`opts.model` else askGrok's `grok-4.3`). A resolved provider whose env key is missing throws `LlmNotConfiguredError` — **never a silent fallback**. Forwards `fetchImpl` only on the openrouter path, `promptCacheKey` only on grok. Also `llmConfigured()` (either key set — the AI-layer runtime gate) / `llmProviderReady(p)` / pure `resolveProvider` / **`llmErrorPayload(err)`** (AI.5 — shared HTTP mapping: `LlmNotConfiguredError`→503 `llm_not_configured`, `GrokApiError`/`OpenRouterApiError`→429/502 `grok_upstream_error`/`openrouter_upstream_error`, else null so routes keep their generic branch). **LIVE (AI.5 + AI.6)** — call sites: replies single+batch, drafter, pillars/draft, voiceExtract, playbook extract-winners, digest, icebreaker. |

It is a COST lever, not a filter — X bills every result in the response BODY, so dropping replies in JS after the fact costs exactly the same; the request is the only place a reply can be made free. lowercases the handle, clamps `text` to `SIGHTING_TEXT_MAX=500`, folds legacy `'hot'`/`'warm'` onto `'sweep'`, `likes`/`verified` absent = null never 0/false (§7.11), `seenAt` defaults to `nowMs` and is **clamped to ≤ now** so a fast client clock can't freeze a row's metrics forever, `sourcePath` must start with `/` and is refused — never rewritten — when a full URL arrives). `derivePostedAt(seenAtMs, ageMin)` (never null: `ageMin: 0` is a real answer). `mergeSightingRow(existing, incoming)` → the column patch, **four** rules each from a different §7 clause: fill-only on `url`/`author`/`verified`/`source_path`/`posted_at`, metrics move only for a **newer-or-equal** sighting (`>=`, see the stamp), band ratchets via the shared `bandStickiness`, and **RQ.1's dismissal clear — `dismissedAt: null` is in the patch ONLY when `incoming.band === 'manual'`** (the ⊕ pin), spread in rather than written as a ternary-`undefined` because drizzle treats an explicitly-`undefined` key as *nothing* on some paths and as NULL on others and this rule cannot depend on which. **A plain re-sighting deliberately does NOT resurrect a dismissed row** — the exact asymmetry `extension/src/shared/radar.ts::mergeSightings` already documents ("ONE exception, and it is the human"), and the server mirror of its `purgeDismissed`. **No db import and no clock of its own** — the write half takes `nowMs`, the read half derives every age from the rows' own timestamps. **RA.3 added the READ half:** `buildSightingViews(rows, cfg, {drafted, replied, people, targets})` → per row `ageMinAtLastSeen` (`lastSeenAt − postedAt`, **null** when `posted_at` is unknown), `vpm` (2dp, null with the age), `admitted` (**tri-state** — `passesSweep` at that age with the config it is GIVEN, so a preset change re-reads history; unknown `verified` refuses, unknown `likes` reads as 0 — the page's own reading), `drafted`/`replied`/`worked`, **`dismissed`** (RQ.3 — straight off `dismissed_at`, orthogonal to `worked`: waving a row off is a decision, not work), `stage` (null for a RETIRED person — the `GET /harvest/affinity` rule verbatim) and `isTarget`; dates out as ISO strings, and a null `url` stays null (a synthesised permalink would erase the unknown, §7.11). `summarizeSightings(views)` → **counts only, never a rate** (§7.19 — the gated funnel is `GET /playbook`'s `timelineFunnel`): `total`/`admitted`/`worked`/**`dismissed`** (RQ.3 — and it deliberately does NOT net out of `unworkedAdmitted`: that counts the replies that were still available, and a dismissal is the choice not to take one)/**`unworkedAdmitted`** (the finding), `byBand`, `bySourcePath` (a null path buckets as `SIGHTING_PATH_UNKNOWN='unknown'`; a real path always starts with `/`), `topHandles` (top 10, handle-asc tie-break so two calls over unchanged data diff clean). **RA.4 added the COMPOSE half and closed two forks:** `sightingVpm(views, ageMin)` (2dp, `max(ageMin,1)` — extracted from `buildSightingViews`, which now calls it) and **`composeDraftSignals(row, nowMs)`** → the `TweetSignals` blob a composed draft carries; `ageMin` is measured from `posted_at` **at compose time**, deliberately NOT the view's `ageMinAtLastSeen`, because the confirm route derives the post time back out as `draftedAt − ageMin` (a draft written hours after the capture would place the post hours late). A null `posted_at` (hand-written row only — the ingest always derives one) falls back to the age since the LAST SIGHTING, a defensible lower bound, and **never to null**: a null `signals` makes the whole draft invisible on rehydrate (D186). `coerceBand` is also **exported now** so the compose route narrows the stored free-text band through the one fold instead of a third copy (§7.27). |

`bestTimeMinN` 1–20 default 3, **`mirrored`** — the only mirrored UI.4 knob), `radar` (`draftTtlH` 6–168; **RC.3:** + `curatedCount` 5–50 default 25, **`mirrored`** — the panel labels the Curate & draft button with it and decides whether the button renders at all; its `max` is asserted EQUAL to `x.ai.batchReplyCap`'s, since the effective size is `min(the two)`), `workers` (`dailyMetricsHourUtc`/`publisherIntervalSec`, both **`appliesOn:'restart'`**; `winnerRereadMinViews` [default from `envNumberDefault('WINNER_REREAD_MIN_VIEWS',500,…)` — override row > env > baked, an out-of-range env value is warned and ignored] / `winnerRereadCap` 0–10, both read per daily run; **XR.1:** + `discoveryExcludeReplies` **boolean, default `true`, `server`** — the registry's FIRST boolean knob, and the one knob here that is a pure money lever: it puts `exclude=replies` on the discovery pull, also read per run so a PATCH binds the next pass and the next manual `POST /posts/reconcile`). **UI.7** group: `band` (all 12 `x.band.*` — `bigViews`/`baitViews`/`earlyReplies`/`midReplies`/`freshMin`/`risingVPM`/`baitVPM`/`watchVPM`/`watchReplyCeiling`/`tooSmallAgeMin`/`tooSmallViews`/`tooSmallVpm`, **every one `mirrored`**, defaults = `BAND` itself, each description carrying the §7.19 ">=100 measured replies" warning; a test asserts the group is exactly `keyof BandThresholds`, so a knob can't be half-exposed). **UI.12** grew `display` with the four Today caps (`doNextCap`/`doNextSnoozeH`/`fansAmberTopN`/`radarDraftCap`, all `mirrored`); **UI.14** with the three list caps (`dossierListLen` 3–25 d5, `channelPostsShown` 3–30 d8, `voiceListLimit` 20–500 d100, all `mirrored`) — the group is now **9 knobs, 7 of them mirrored**, and the two that stay `server` (`sparklineDays`/`leaderCount`) are the ones the brief applies before the panel sees them. **CQ.1** group: `cannon` (`x.cannon.scoreMin`/`maxAgeMin`/`redAgeMin`/`placedTarget`, **all four `mirrored`** — the page's capture arm and the panel's Cannon view decide with the same numbers the server does; defaults imported from `CANNON` in `src/shared/cannon.ts`, never retyped, and a group-shape test asserts the group is exactly `keyof CannonThresholds`, the `band`-group precedent). `placedTarget` is **display-only** and its description says so: the counter's real target comes from the active `replies` commitment / doctrine (`routes/radar.ts::placed-today`), and a second owner of that number is how the head and the quest start disagreeing. **OH.1** group: `identity` (`x.identity.selfHandle` — **`string`, default `''`, `mirrored`**; the ONLY knob whose job is to name the subject rather than tune a decision, which is why it renders FIRST). It exists because the server has no other way to learn the handle: `SELF_X_USER_ID` is a numeric id and `account_snapshots` stores no username. A `getMe()`-stamped schema column was considered and rejected (a migration plus a fresh install waiting until 03:00 UTC, to save a single-user system from typing its own handle once). **No handle regex beyond the registry's `not_a_string`** — `parseIngestRow` already owns handle shape, and a refused save is worse than a typo the user can see; consumers normalize at read time (`routes/playbook.ts::configuredSelfHandle`). Unset ⇒ every own-activity read answers its EMPTY shape (§7.11). **RS.1** group: `sweep` (the eleven `x.sweep.*` — `minViews`/`maxViews`/`minLikes`/`maxLikes`/`minReplies`/`maxReplies`/`maxAgeMin`/`verifiedOnly`/`campedBypass`/`circleBypass`/`autoStopMin`, **every one `mirrored`**, defaults imported from `SWEEP` in `src/shared/radarSweep.ts` and never retyped, group-shape test asserts exactly `keyof SweepConfig`). Three of them are `boolean` (the `x.workers.discoveryExcludeReplies` exemplar). **This is the group with NO server consumer at all** — no route, worker or loader reads `x.sweep.*`; the content script does, off the mirrored blob, which makes `mirrored` the mechanism here rather than a convenience (the `x.display.*` caps are the precedent). Ranges: the six metric knobs `0..1_000_000`, `maxAgeMin` `1..1440` (**floor 1 — the one maximum where `0` is out of range rather than "no ceiling"**, and its description says so), `autoStopMin` `1..240`. Every description ends with the §7.19 recalibrate-at-n≥100-swept-rows line. **SW.1** grew `sweep` to **13** with two CONTENT gates (`x.sweep.media` enum `any|with|without` d`any`, `x.sweep.excludeAds` boolean d`true`, both **`mirrored`**). **OU.3** group: `outliers` (the six `x.outliers.*` — `minFaves` d400, `minRetweets` d0, `minReplies` d0 (all three `0..100_000`, where **`0` is a real value meaning "omit the operator"**, not "unknown"), `sinceDays` `1..365` d30 (**floor 1 — a zero-day window would put `since:` at today**), `lang` `string` d`''`, `sort` `enum ['live','top']` d**`top`**). **Every one is `server` and NONE is mirrored, and that is the group's defining property**: these are *defaults handed to a form*, not rules anything enforces — the panel receives them already resolved through `GET /x/searches/defaults` (OU.4) and has no client-side decision to make off them, so §7.24's seven-edit mirrored move collapses to the server three. Two carve-outs the plan text did not have: `sort`'s default is the **product** default and the `saved_searches.sort` column default (`'live'`) must never stand in for it (D200/D201); and `lang` is a plain `string` rather than an `enum` because `''` is the shipped value and an enum has no blank option — membership in `SEARCH_LANGS` is enforced one layer up (OU.4 drops an unknown code with a `warn`), and the knob's `description` **interpolates the allowlist from the constant** so a code added to `SEARCH_LANGS` can never go unlisted in the gear (asserted). This makes `registry.ts` import `src/shared/searchQuery.ts` — the plan forbade it on a cycle-risk theory, but that module has **zero imports**, so the risk does not exist and the `CANNON`/`SWEEP` imports two lines up are the precedent (D204). **Registry total: 16 groups / 69 knobs; the mirrored set is 33** (79 → 61 + 17→15 groups + 44→31 mirrored at XD.1 when the `band` and `mentions` groups went; 61→63 + 31→33 at SW.1; **63→69 + 15→16 groups, mirrored UNMOVED at 33, at OU.3** — recounted from `SETTINGS_REGISTRY`, not carried forward; do not trust a stale number). Group render order = **identity**→doctrine→quests→people→followups→pinned→digest→gates→radar→**sweep**→**cannon**→**outliers**→workers→budgets→ai→display. `withMe`/`withoutMe`/`totalMeasured`, clone of relationship lift + a `totalMeasured` field for the partition invariant)**, **model effectiveness (`buildModelEffectiveness`, AI.12 — posted replies bucketed by raw `reply_drafts.model` string [`/` = provider, never parsed]; `{cells: ModelCell[], totalMeasured}`, cells most-sampled-first, each independently gated; **no lift line** — buckets only, no baseline pair; the OpenRouter-experiment judge)**, **timeline opportunity funnel (`buildTimelineFunnel`, HV.5 — §12, NOT §11 which AI.12 took; `TimelineSeenRow{tweetId,views,comments,text,tweetTimeMs|null,capturedAtMs}` + `deriveTimelineBand` [ageMin = capturedAt−tweetTime, vpm = views/max(ageMin,1), bait = `textLooksLikeReplyBait`, fed to shared `classifyBand`] → `{cells: FunnelCell[], totalSeen, totalReplied}`; `TimelineBand = Band | 'unknown'` where **`'unknown'` = no tweet time (no age ⇒ no velocity ⇒ nothing to classify) and NEVER folds into the real `null` band**; rows are deduped to their **first sighting** (earliest `capturedAtMs`) inside the pure fn too, so a re-scrolled viral thread can't re-band itself; per-cell gate on `seen`, `rate = replied/seen` null under it)**, **post format (`buildFormatEffectiveness`, SC.5 — §13; own originals bucketed by `classifyFormat(text)` at read time, cells in `POST_FORMATS` CASCADE order [fixed, not most-sampled-first: a diagnostic table keeps its rows where you left them] and only for formats that occur; `{cells, totalPosted, totalMeasured}`, **no lift line** — 14 buckets have no baseline pair, so the useful comparison is a format against `substance`; the one cell with real n on day one, because `posts_published.text` is NOT NULL)**, **the coach's own judge (`buildCoachScoreEffectiveness`, SC.5 — §14; the SAME originals keyed two ways: all four `CoachBand`s worst→best [always rendered, an empty band is an honest zero] AND `clean`/`flagged` on `counts.fix>0`, which is D152(b) — the band is a WEAK key since `standard` is a mean over ~20 rules, so a 90-scoring draft can still carry a red fix row. `spread` = highest ÷ lowest GATED band with `spreadBands:{high,low}` NAMING the pair [on a real corpus it is rarely top-vs-rework], `fixSpread` = clean ÷ flagged, both null unless both sides gate. Bands are NOT re-cut here — `scoreDraft` owns the cut points or the cell grades a different number than the Composer showed)**. **Measured 2026-07-27 over 109 prod originals: format = substance 47% / list 15% / cta 14% / story 10%; coach band = top 97%, ship 3%, rework/almost ZERO, every post ≥83, and the only fixes firing are `url_cost` (6) + `answerable_question` (1) — i.e. the band axis is a near-constant on this account and the fix axis is essentially 'did it carry a URL'. Binds SC.8 (the score is a weak feature) and JD.7.**, **the LLM judge's own falsification cell (`buildJudgeEffectiveness`, JD.7 — §15; `JudgeRow{verdictBand: JudgeVerdictLabel|null, outcome}` → all four bands worst→best (`JUDGE_VERDICT_ORDER`) which partition the JUDGED rows only, `unjudged` as a SIBLING bucket (§7.11 — never judged, or judged then edited; expected to be the biggest row for months), and `approved`/`rejected` = the same judged rows split by `deriveApproved`, which is the SC.5 clean/flagged move: a 2-way split gates at half the sample a 4-way one needs. `spread`/`spreadBands` and `approvedSpread` follow the coach cell's shape exactly. The band arrives resolved — hashing is the loader's job, so this file stays crypto-free)**, **my own harvested replies (`buildOwnReplyPerformance`, OH.2 — §16; `OwnReplyRow[]` × `rosterByHandle: Map<handle, language|null>` → `{totalMeasured, totalViews, viewsPerReply, bands, latency, crowding, arms}`). Four axes, edges taken **VERBATIM** from `x-growth-plan-v3.md` §2.2–§2.4 so the tables read against the same cuts as the 1,000-reply reference corpus, and deliberately NOT reusing the neighbours they resemble: `OWN_REPLY_BANDS` (`<1k`/`1k-10k`/`10k-50k`/`50k-200k`/`200k+`/`unknown`) bands one POST's views where `AUTHOR_SIZE_BUCKETS` bands an author's followers (a `100k+` ceiling would hide the finding that `200k+` carries 56.7% of yield); `OWN_REPLY_LATENCY_BUCKETS` (`<15m`/`15-60m`/`1-6h`/`6-24h`/`>24h`/`unknown`) is age-at-POST over every harvested reply where `LATENCY_BUCKETS` is age-at-DRAFT over `reply_drafts` — **§8 splits `>6h` in two because those rows behave nothing alike**, and negative age is CLAMPED to 0 (X renders relative times, so a reply can read a minute "before" its parent — scrape noise belongs in the fastest bucket, not in `unknown`); `OWN_REPLY_CROWD_BUCKETS` (`<10`/`10-50`/`50-200`/`200+`/`unknown`) on `parentComments`. `OWN_REPLY_ARMS` is **post-hoc and derived, never stamped** — `ownReplyArm(parentHandle, parentText, roster)` → `roster-ja`/`roster-en` (handle in `cannon_targets`, split by `resolveLanguageProfile(language)?.code === 'ja'`) else `off-roster-nonlatin`/`off-roster-en` (`detectScript(parentText)`), and a NULL handle is `unknown` not `off-roster-*` ("off roster" is a claim about a handle you had to have seen). The reason is a measurement, not a preference: **0 of the first 98 harvested replies matched a `reply_drafts` row** (all hand-typed outside the pipeline), so the drafting path cannot supply an arm and never will. Cells (`OwnReplyCell`) carry `n`/`totalViews`/`avgYield`/`avgParentViews`/`sharePct`/`sufficient`; this family **averages** where the rest of the file takes medians (the reference corpus is quoted as means), an insufficient cell keeps its counts and NULLS both averages, and `sharePct` is computed over ALL views **including insufficient cells** so the column still sums to 100. `unknown` is its own bucket on all four axes, never folded into a neighbour (§7.11). Rows dedupe by `tweetId` here too — **LATEST wins**, belt-and-suspenders behind the loader's SQL, and the opposite direction from `buildTimelineFunnel`'s earliest-wins)**, **the ranker's own falsification cell (`buildRankerScoreEffectiveness`, XR.4 — §15b; `RankerPostRow{text, counts: MeasuredCounts, feats?: DraftFeatures, outcome}` → `{cells, contentCells, totalPosted, totalMeasured, totalScoredE, spread, spreadQuartiles, contentSpread, contentSpreadQuartiles}`. QUARTILES, not a fixed vocabulary: cut points come from the sample itself per call (`calibrate-ranker.ts`'s quantile, deliberately the same one), TIES ARE KEPT TOGETHER so an empty quartile is possible and is OMITTED rather than rendered as a zero row, and each `RankerScoreCell` carries `quartile` 1..4 [NOT the array index], its observed `range{lo,hi}` and `medianScore`. `spread`/`spreadQuartiles` are the `spreadBands` discipline verbatim — highest ÷ lowest GATED quartile, naming which two. **`cells` is E and `contentCells` is C, and only ONE of them is evidence:** E reads the row's own counts, and views is E's denominator while rate falls as reach rises, so E is mildly ANTI-correlated with views before any content effect — measured over a real 481-post profile harvest, C spread **1.71x** against E's **0.50x**. `totalScoredE` < `totalPosted` is normal: a row the DOM caught with no view count has no rate and therefore no E, which is not a zero (§7.11). Takes the ACTIVE lexicon for `buildCoachScoreEffectiveness`'s exact reason)** |

Verified non-forked against prod: both sides return the same 14 handles. **GT.7 added `ReciprocityScope.asOf`** — the stage half additionally requires a rung reached BEFORE that instant (`stageUpdatedAt` is written only on an actual rung change, so it reads as "when they became this"; null ⇒ predates ⇒ in). The single path is the same function over a one-element set, which is why it collapses to the plain precedence. | `digest.ts` | `GET /digest?week=&tzOffsetMin=&refresh=&factsOnly=` (cached per week; degrades to facts on LLM failure). **ME.5:** facts carry `goals` — `loadGoals(now)` = active `me_goals` × latest `account_snapshots` followers via `resolveGoals`, null when none. **AI.6:** `loadPromptSafe('digest')` → `buildDigestInput(facts, prompt.body)` + `askLLM` (defaults low/700/0.7, `prompt.cacheKey` replaces the static `stratus-digest`); the no-key degrade + catch classify to `llm_not_configured`/`grok_<status>`/`openrouter_<status>`/`llm_parse_error`/`llm_failed` (gate = `llmConfigured()`; the extension `Digest.tsx` matcher moved to `llm_not_configured`). **GR.9:** `loadFacts(start, end, weekKey, tzOffsetMin, now)` also assembles the scorecard inputs — `daysWithOriginal` = distinct `localDayKey(postedAt, tz)` over the week's non-reply `posts_published` (`postedAt` added to that select, never reaching the facts JSON), `daysInWeek` = 7 once the week is over else the elapsed days, `repliesTargetWeek` = the ACTIVE `replies` commitment's `dailyTarget` else `doctrine.replyTargetMin`, **× daysInWeek** (same resolution as GR.8's quests; the debt half of `loadCommitmentsWithDebt` is unused here — the loader is imported so "which commitment is active" has one reading), `goalVerdicts` = active goals off **`loadGoalsWithPacing`**, and `loadPrevScore(weekKey)` reads last week's cached `digests.facts.scorecard.score` (missing/ungraded → null delta, never a comparison against 0). **Consequence: generating a digest now WRITES** (the goals loader's `active→achieved|missed` flip) — the fifth read-that-writes after `/radar/drafts`, `/following/queue`, `/x/goals` and `/x/brief`; the cache path returns before it, so re-opening Sunday's digest doesn't re-flip, but `x_digest` (factsOnly) does. |
| `brief`/`streaks` | streak upsert happens inside `GET /brief` (idempotent per local day). |
| `images.ts` | `POST /images/generate` (n≤2; HARD daily budget `x.budgets.imageDailyUsd` read per call → 429 before spend, `0` disables generation; returns data: URLs). |
| `assets.ts` | `POST /assets` (≤2MB), `GET /assets` (metadata only), `GET /assets/:id/png` (bytes), `DELETE /assets/:id`. |
| `data.ts` | `GET /data/tables`, `GET /data/:table`, `POST /data/query` — S1 read-only; plus the `explorer` router mounted at root **outside bearer** (data-free shells, §7.21): `GET /explorer` (S1) and **A3.13** `GET /writer` (the Writer page — both lazy `Bun.file`-cache `public/*.html`; adding `/writer` needed no `index.ts` change, the router was already `app.route('/', explorer)`). |
| `settings.ts` | UI.1 (mounted next to `data`): `GET /settings` (groups + value + isDefault), `GET /settings/values?scope=mirrored` (flat mirror payload), `PATCH /settings` (per-key validated, all-or-nothing → 400 `unknown_setting`/`invalid_setting_value`), `POST /settings/reset` (`{keys?,group?}`). Always mounted, $0; **landed inert — no store consumer yet** (UI.2–7 wire them). Registry size after UI.12: **14 groups / 57 knobs, 23 `mirrored`**. |

Shared/other: `GET /healthz` (public), `GET/cost/today`, `GET /cost/daily`, `POST /grok/ask`, `POST /mcp` (JSON-RPC; GET/DELETE→405).

**RC.10 reply-craft delta for §3 (the rows above predate the lane; this is the current wiring):**

- `src/shared/replyMode.ts` (**RC.2, NEW**) — dependency-free canonical home of `PersonaUse`, six `ReplyMode`s, the ordered five-value `REPLY_ANGLES`, `ANGLE_VOCABULARY_WIDENED_AT='2026-08-08'`, universal opening bans, `detectReplyMode`, `resolveModeId`, and `containsLaneNoun`. Detection uses distinct weighted markers (one strong or two weak), hard wire-prefix/domain overrides, strict-leader semantics, real English/Japanese corpus markers, and returns `null` on no vote/tie — never `general`. Every range/move is an opening guess; recalibrate at ≥30 harvested replies per mode. Zero runtime dependencies so the extension can inline it.
- `src/x/replies/mode.ts` (**RC.3/RC.5, NEW**) — the one async resolver both single and batch call over the same target array: explicit override → `curatedMode` → `cannonTopicForSafe` → `detectReplyMode` → `GENERAL_MODE`, returning `source:'explicit'|'curated'|'roster'|'detected'|'fallback'`. One topic SELECT per distinct handle; mode is per-post, deliberately unlike language's all-or-nothing set. `trimToModeAngles` is the route-level product contract and preserves the paid payload if every label is outside the room.
- `src/x/replies/winners.ts` (**RC.6, NEW**) — `$0` measured few-shot selector over `latestOwnReplyRows`: up to five unique ≥50-view replies per requested room, latest 21 days, language-matched, parent-required, current topic-pin/detection attribution, fallback rows excluded, yield-desc. `loadReplyWinnersSafe` never blocks the paid path. Rendered at the tail because selection varies by room; no `{{REPLY_WINNERS}}` token was added to the cacheable head.
- `src/x/replies/prompt.ts` (**RC.1/RC.4–RC.6 current**) — `ReplyAngle` now aliases the shared five-value union; schema builders accept a narrowed `angles` enum while the exported constants remain the full-vocabulary defaults. `renderModeClause`, `renderBatchTweet`'s `MODE:` line, `renderBatchModeNote` (distinct rooms once), and `renderReplyWinnersBlock` are server-owned rendered values. One room narrows a single schema; a batch schema takes the union. `renderLanguageClause` wins the angle sentence when a non-English profile resolves. Both parsers accept all five labels but never enforce product count; routes trim after parse.
- `src/x/replies/curate.ts` + `src/x/prompts/registry.ts` (**RC.8 current**) — the `reply-curate` rubric is now topic-agnostic answerability: concrete hook regardless of lane, plus `unanswerable without fabrication` as the new negative. `CURATE_SCHEMA` adds required `mode` with the six ids; `parseCurateScores` normalizes a recognized id and degrades an invented one to `null` without losing the score. The scored response carries it; the panel attaches it as `curatedMode` only to kept rows. `selectCurated` stays id-only. Prompt-key count stays 16.
- `src/x/routes/replies.ts` (**RC.3/RC.5–RC.8 current**) — accepts top-level `mode?` (validated before work) and per-tweet `curatedMode?` shape only. Both routes resolve room inside the refusal ladder and echo `mode`/`modeSource` per reply; single stamps both into `contextSnapshot`, batch stamps the resolved mode into each rendered tweet. The single schema uses that room's angles; mixed batch uses the union then trims per tweet. `personaUse !== 'full'` skips the lane-specific specificity gate and its paid retry; primary becomes the room's first angle. Winners are loaded once per distinct room. Curation's kept `{mode}` becomes `curatedMode` on the next call.
- `src/x/playbook.ts` + `src/x/routes/playbook.ts` (**RC.9 current**) — own-harvest performance now includes mode, opening, opening × mode, corpus/cell capture basis points, and contamination. Topic-pin → detection → `unknown` at read time; never fallback-general. `OwnReplyRosterEntry` carries language + topic in one fresh map. Contamination is lane nouns only where `personaUse !== 'full'`, with denominator/rate and contaminated-vs-clean yields independently gated. `GET /x/playbook` returns these additions under the existing `ownReplyPerformance` slice.
- `src/x/routes/radar.ts` (**RC.8 current**) — `RadarBatchTweet.curatedMode` is the sole curation-to-drafting room hint. Unlike `band`/`signals`/`curationScore`, it is not persisted measurement metadata and never renders directly; only the resolver-produced `BatchTweet.mode` reaches the prompt.

Row absent = the shipped default in `prompts/registry.ts` applies; restore = DELETE; `customized` = row presence. No seed by design (a later-deploy default improvement applies unless overridden). Explorer/MCP-visible — never store secrets. |
| `cannonTargets` (L1107) | **CQ.2 (NEW)** — the camped arbitrage roster: `handle` PK (lowercased, no `@`), `display_name?`, `language?` (null = English — the arm this handle belongs to, read by CQ.7's per-batch language pick), `score`/`median_views`/`median_comments` (real, **`score` null = never scored, NEVER 0** — §7.11, and 0 would be a real verdict), `sample_n` (default 0), `scored_at?` (ms; set even when the score is null — "we looked and there wasn't enough" is a distinct fact), `active` (1 = camped, 0 = bench — the §9 "keep 5 bench candidates" arm; membership for the gate carve-out and the glance flag is `active` only), `notes?`, `added_at`/`updated_at`. Index `(active, score)` = the review sort. **`score` is STORED rather than read-time and that is a deliberate §7.12 exception, for reasons the schema records:** it is a weekly-cadence aggregate over a 30-post window per handle, it must be *comparable across a review session* (a score that drifts between two reads of the same list is not a review), and `scored_at` is what makes staleness legible. The per-**sighting** cannon score stays read-time and is stored nowhere. Deliberately NOT a flag on `voice_authors` (that is the swipe-file roster — mixing them would force every `voice.ts` reader to start filtering) and deliberately NOT the 2–10× target set (`loadTargetHandles()` never sees these handles). **`radar_drafts.band` widens to accept `'cannon'` with NO migration** — free-text column, the RU.8 `'manual'` / GT.8 `'roster'` precedent. |
| `savedSearches` (L1270) | **OU.2 (NEW)** — named outlier hunts for the Outliers tab: `id` uuid PK, `name`, `query` (the STRUCTURED `SearchQuery` params as JSON, stored NORMALIZED through `parseSearchQuery` — the `reply_lists.humanizer` discipline, so the read path never re-validates), `sort` (`'live'`\|`'top'`), `pinned`, `last_run_at?` (**null = never run**, §7.11 — stamped by `POST /x/searches/:id/run` and only when the stored query still compiles), `created_at`/`updated_at`. **The compiled string is never stored** — it cannot be loaded back into the form, and a compiler fix (an operator X renames) could then never reach rows already saved; it is derived on every read. **`query` is a plain `text`, NOT `text({ mode: 'json' })`**: drizzle parses a json column during result mapping inside `.all()`, so one out-of-band-edited row throws where no route code catches it and takes the whole list with it — raw text lets the reader `JSON.parse` per row and degrade that row to `compiled: null`, visible and therefore deletable. **A table and not an `app_settings` blob**, and `settings/sweepPresets.ts` does NOT transfer: a sweep preset is snapshotted server-side from already-validated registry values and never posted by a client, which is what makes loading one blind safe — a saved search IS client-supplied structure, so it needs the strict parse in, the tolerant parse out, and per-row identity for PATCH/DELETE. No seed and **no index by design** (a single-user table of tens of rows sorted in memory needs none; an unused index is a claim about scale this feature does not have). **`sort`'s column default `'live'` is NOT the product default** — `x.outliers.sort` (`top`) is, and OU.4 resolves an omitted `sort` from the knob. **OU.4 is the table's only consumer** (`routes/searches.ts`), and it stores the JSON **without** `sort` so the column is that field's single authority. |

Migrations `0000`–`0028` — **the next migration owns `0029`** (see the RC.10 and TH.1 deltas below for `0027`/`0028`; historical detail follows: **`0026_pink_steve_rogers` CQ.2 — exactly one `CREATE TABLE cannon_targets` + one `CREATE INDEX cannon_targets_active_score_idx`, DDL-only, no seed, nothing else touched; verified by reading the emitted SQL and by a fresh `:memory:` boot still reporting the 3 `content_pillars` seed rows, the RC.2 read-back discipline**; prior: **`0025_curvy_edwin_jarvis` RC.2 — exactly 1 `ALTER TABLE radar_drafts ADD curation_score integer`, DDL-only, no seed, no index, nothing else touched; `git diff` over `src/db/migrations/` showed only the `_journal.json` append, and a fresh `:memory:` boot reports 18 `radar_drafts` columns + the 3 `content_pillars` seed rows still there.** `0024_soft_leopardon` JD.4 — 1 CREATE TABLE (`draft_judgments`) + 1 index (`draft_judgments_text_hash_idx`), DDL-only, no seed, no FK, nothing touched on existing tables.** `0023_slimy_night_thrasher` A3.11 — 1 CREATE TABLE (`articles`) + 1 index (`articles_status_updated_idx`), DDL-only, no seed, no FK, nothing touched on existing tables. `0022_chilly_tomas` A3.9 — 1 CREATE TABLE (`dm_drafts`) + FK to `people.handle` + 1 index, DDL-only, no seed. `0021_square_iron_monger` A3.2 — 1 CREATE TABLE (`audience_activity`) + 1 index, DDL-only, no seed. `0020_tidy_thunderbolts` GR.7 — 1 CREATE TABLE (`commitments`) + 2 nullable `me_goals` ADD COLUMNs, DDL-only, no seed; nullable adds are the only safe way to widen a live table on SQLite. `0019_messy_blue_shield` GR.1 `following`+`following_runs` — 2 CREATE TABLEs + 1 index, DDL-only, no seed, nothing touched on existing tables. `following` is created BEFORE the `following_runs` it FKs to; SQLite resolves FK targets at DML time, not CREATE time, so the order is harmless. `0018_flimsy_captain_universe` RL.2 `reply_lists`+`reply_list_items`+`reply_list_uses` — 3 CREATE TABLEs + 2 indexes, DDL-only, no seed, nothing touched on existing tables; `0013` app_settings, `0014` RU.2 reply `source` + radar `variants`/`model`/`reply_draft_id`, `0015` N0.1 `niches` table + seed INSERT + nullable `niche` on content_pillars/channels + `UPDATE … SET niche='builder'` backfills — the seed/backfill DML was hand-appended after generate, `0016_high_miek` ME.1 `me_entries`+`me_goals` — DDL-only, no seed, `0017_misty_zeigeist` AI.3 `prompt_overrides` — single CREATE TABLE, no seed by design). Workflow: edit schema → `bun run db:generate` → **inspect the SQL** (drizzle drops seed INSERTs; keep them idempotent) → boot/`deploy.sh` migrates. (biome now ignores `src/db/migrations` — UI.1, D11/D13.)

**RC.10 database delta (supersedes the historical migration list above):** table count stays **42**. Migration head is **`0027_bizarre_the_captain.sql`**, exactly `ALTER TABLE cannon_targets ADD topic text;` — nullable, no seed, no backfill, no index, and the generated SQL was inspected. `cannon_targets.topic` is a normalized `ReplyMode.id` on route writes; null/unknown means the resolver falls through, not that the handle is `general`, and inactive rows still answer because benching changes capture membership rather than the account's room. `reply_drafts.variants` and `radar_drafts.angle/variants` need no migration for `observation`/`question` (JSON/free text, no CHECK); storage remains loose for legacy/CLI rows while prompt/route types are strict. Single drafts stamp `contextSnapshot.mode`, `modeSource`, and optional `winners` count before insert, so measurement reads what the model actually saw rather than re-resolving history. `radar_drafts` does not add a mode column: the live Radar sighting owns the display chip, and `curatedMode` is a transient input, not measurement storage.

**OU.2 database delta (current, supersedes the RQ.1 delta below):** table count **43 → 44**. Migration head is **`0031_sharp_screwball.sql`** — exactly one `CREATE TABLE saved_searches` (8 columns), **no index, no seed, no FK**, nothing touched on an existing table. **The next migration owns `0032`.** Verified by reading the emitted SQL, by `git diff --stat src/db/migrations/` showing only the `_journal.json` append (the `.sql` and its snapshot are new files), and by a fresh `:memory:` boot reporting the 8 expected columns, **44 tables**, and the 3 `content_pillars` seed rows still there. The one index `PRAGMA index_list` reports is SQLite's own `sqlite_autoindex_saved_searches_1` (`origin: 'pk'`, `sql: null`) for the TEXT primary key — identical to `reply_lists`, and **not** a declared index; check `origin` before concluding a no-index table grew one. Nothing reads or writes the table yet — OU.4 is its only consumer.

**RQ.1 database delta (current, supersedes the RA.1 delta below):** table count stays **43**. Migration head is **`0030_famous_wrecker.sql`**, exactly `ALTER TABLE radar_sightings ADD dismissed_at integer;` — nullable, no seed, no backfill, **no index** (`SIGHTING_SCAN_CAP` already bounds the queue read and this is a single-user DB), and the generated SQL was inspected: `git diff --stat src/db/migrations/` showed only the new file, its snapshot and the `_journal.json` append, and a fresh `:memory:` boot reports **17 `radar_sightings` columns** and the 3 `content_pillars` seed rows still there. **The next migration owns `0031`.** `dismissed_at` is **null = never dismissed** (§7.11 — that is the column's whole vocabulary, and it is why no backfill was needed: every pre-existing row is truthfully "never dismissed"). Written by `PATCH /x/radar/sightings` under an `isNull` guard (a ratchet — a re-dismiss re-stamps nothing) and cleared by exactly one thing: a `manual`-band re-ingest, i.e. the ⊕ pin, through `mergeSightingRow`'s fourth rule. Read by `GET /x/radar/sightings?queue=true` and surfaced as `SightingView.dismissed` + a `SightingSummary.dismissed` count on every read.

**RA.1 database delta (supersedes the TH.1 delta below):** table count **42 → 43**. Migration head is **`0029_blushing_expediter.sql`** — one `CREATE TABLE radar_sightings` + `CREATE INDEX radar_sightings_last_seen_idx (last_seen_at)` + `CREATE INDEX radar_sightings_handle_idx (handle, last_seen_at)`, DDL-only, no seed, no FK, nothing touched on an existing table; verified by reading the emitted SQL, by `git diff --stat src/db/migrations/` showing only the `_journal.json` append, and by a fresh `:memory:` boot reporting 16 `radar_sightings` columns and the 3 `content_pillars` seed rows still there (**RQ.1 took it to 17 — see the delta above; `0030` is spent and the next migration owns `0031`**). The row: `radar_sightings` — **the Radar's sighting corpus, one row per tweet, UPSERTED.** `tweet_id` PK, `url?`, `handle` (lowercased), `author?`, `text` (clamped 500), `band` (free text like `radar_drafts.band`, so an old build's `'hot'`/`'warm'` folds onto `'sweep'` at ingest with no migration), `views`/`replies` notNull, `likes?`, `bait` notNull, `verified?`, `posted_at?` (derived once from `seenAt − ageMin`, then fill-only — age is a moving number, the post time is a fact, and this is what keeps `POST /radar/drafts/:tweetId/confirm`'s `draftedAt − ageMin` landing on the true post time hours after capture), `source_path?` (the x.com pathname — `/home`, `/search`, a list, a profile: the one thing the passive corpus structurally cannot answer), `first_seen_at`/`last_seen_at`, `seen_count` (default 1), **`dismissed_at?` (RQ.1)**. **Deliberately NOT a second `harvest_rows` series** (that table owns the /home metric curve; this answers "what did my sweep admit"), and `vpm`/`person_tier` are **deliberately not columns** — both are the server's own read-time answers (views/age; `people` + the target roster), so a stored client copy would fork a rule the server owns (§7.12/§7.16). No FK (a sighting is usually a stranger). Retention is a lazy 60-day prune on the ingest path, like `prunePassiveRuns`. **No `people`/`person_events` write from this ingest and nothing near `mentions`** — HV.1 decision 6, restated so nobody "improves" it later: exposure is not interaction.

**TH.1 database delta:** table count was **42** — no new table. Migration head is **`0028_glorious_chat.sql`**, exactly `ALTER TABLE harvest_runs ADD root_tweet_id text;` + `CREATE INDEX harvest_runs_root_idx ON harvest_runs (root_tweet_id, created_at);` — nullable, no seed, no backfill, and the generated SQL was inspected (the `content_pillars` seed in `0000` is intact). **The next migration owns `0029`.** Nothing outside the two TH.2 reads selects on the column, so the rollback is deleting three route blocks, two MCP tools and one `attachThreadCaptureButton(...)` call — the captured rows then sit inert behind a `mode` no consumer selects.

## 5. Extension — `extension/` (own package.json, Vite + React, MV3)

**Build:** two passes (`vite.config.ts`) — content script first as self-contained **IIFE** (`content.js`; classic script, no imports allowed), then side panel + background as ES modules. Shared modules used by content.ts get inlined. Out-of-tree server modules reach the extension via **re-export shims**: `extension/src/replyBand.ts` → `src/shared/replyBand.ts`, `extension/src/channelSuggest.ts` → `src/shared/channelSuggest.ts`, `extension/src/shared/activeTimes.ts` → `src/shared/activeTimes.ts` (A3.1 — this one also ADDS the DOM extractor on top of the re-export; tsconfig lists all **six** in `include`), `extension/src/postCoach.ts` → `src/shared/postCoach.ts` (SC.3), `extension/src/postFormat.ts` → `src/shared/postFormat.ts` (**SC.5** — the Playbook's format table renders `FORMAT_LABELS` from the canonical cascade; SC.6's cooldown chip takes `classifyFormat` from the same shim), `extension/src/judge.ts` → `src/shared/judge.ts` (**JD.2** — shipped with the canonical module, unconsumed until **JD.6**, which finally bundles it: `JudgePanel.tsx` imports the values and `shared/types.ts` the `JudgeVerdict` the two response types extend. A shim with no importer is typechecked but NOT bundled, so it costs nothing and cannot be forgotten later; `grep -F 'Stranger answerability' dist/sidepanel.js` is the check that it actually inlined), `extension/src/humanize.ts` → `src/shared/humanize.ts` (**HM.1** — consumed on arrival: `ReplyLists.tsx` deleted its local `jitterOdds` and imports it here; `grep -c 'come out changed' dist/sidepanel.js` is the inline check), `extension/src/cannon.ts` → `src/shared/cannon.ts` (**CQ.1** — content.ts's capture arm + `shared/radar.ts::cannonQueue`), `extension/src/language.ts` → `src/shared/language.ts` (**ML.1** — `Replies.tsx`'s weighted counter and the RTL/`maxChars` read; `grep -F 'weightedLength' dist/sidepanel.js` is the inline check), `extension/src/replyMode.ts` → `src/shared/replyMode.ts` (**RC.2**), `extension/src/radarSweep.ts` → `src/shared/radarSweep.ts` (**RS.1** — the capture arm, the on-page chip and `Radar.tsx`'s Start/Stop all read the one admission rule; `grep -F 'radar:sweep' dist/content.js` is the inline check). **`tsconfig.app.json` `include` lists ELEVEN shared files today** — counted from the array at RS.6. This sentence has been wrong twice (it read "seven" through CQ and "NINE" through RC, each time while a shim already sat in the file unlisted here); **count the `include` array, do not trust a remembered number, including this one.** A bare re-export goes at `extension/src/` top level; only a shim that ADDS to its re-export lives under `extension/src/shared/`.

**Manifest:** side panel + background service worker + content script on x.com/twitter.com. Permissions: sidePanel, storage, clipboardWrite/Read, contextMenus, alarms, notifications.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|

One HTTP transport: `ApiRequest` message channel — the only Authorization-header owner (incl. `binary` for asset blobs). Rankmap cache (10min TTL, S0.3). C7 launch alarms (`chrome.alarms`, +90s grace, liveness verify, notification). **A3.8 manual-post reminders** (own `manualChain`/`enqueueManual` — a distinct session-key family): a sibling `syncManualAlarms()` alongside `syncLaunchAlarms()` at all three launch triggers fetches `?status=manual&from=now−30min&to=now+24h` → `computeManualAlarms` → one `stratus-manual:<id>` alarm AT `scheduledFor` (no grace/retry); `parseManualAlarm` dispatches in `onAlarm` BEFORE `parseLaunchAlarm`; `handleManualFire` re-GETs the row and, only if still `manual`, `mergeManualDue`-writes the `manual:due` entry (dedup by postId, cap 5) + fires a `stratus-manual-note:<id>` notification (`manualNotificationText`); `stratus/manual-dismiss {postId}`→`dismissManualDue`; the notification-click handler opens the panel for the manual prefix too. A non-ok response keeps the last good blob and does NOT advance the stamp, so readers fall back to baked defaults and the next trigger retries. **RQ.2 — `markSightingsDismissedOnServer(tweetIds)`**, a sibling to `markDraftsOnServer` directly beneath it and copied from it exactly (the same `MAX_DRAFT_PATCH_IDS` 200-id chunk loop — one constant, because the reason for 200 is identical — the same `void handleApiRequest(...).then(warn, warn)`, the same `unconfigured` silence, the same *never retried*), PATCHing `/x/radar/sightings {tweetIds, dismissed: true}`. Called in the `isRadarDismiss` handler beside the existing `markDraftsOnServer(msg.tweetIds, 'expired')` and **before** `enqueueRadar(...)`, fire-and-forget so it can never precede or block the buffer write in effect (§7.8/§7.24). **One call site covers all four dismissal paths** — the ✕, **Clear**, `consumeQueue`'s leftovers after a drafting pass, and the curate pass's drops all funnel through `stratus/radar-dismiss`. What it fixes: `markDraftsOnServer` only touches rows a draft already created, so a ✕ on a never-drafted tweet was invisible to the server and `/radar-analyst` re-surfaced it (measured 35 in the panel vs 55 in the corpus). **RA.5 — `rehydrateSightings` no longer skips a tweetId the buffer already holds.** It still never REPLACES a live row (the skip's actual rule: a fresh capture's signals beat an hours-old draft row's, and `mergeSightings` would let the stale copy win) — it attaches `reply` + `variants` onto the existing row, the shape `attachReplies` writes. Until RA.4 the only writer of `radar_drafts` was the Grok batch, which attaches on the way back, so "already held" meant "already drafted"; `x_radar_draft_reply` composes for tweets sitting in the live queue, and the plain skip made RA.5's **Fetch drafts** answer `up to date` with a draft on the server. A row already showing that exact `replyText` is left untouched and uncounted, so a second click stays honest and every pre-RA.4 path is a byte-identical no-op. Return value is now "rows that entered **or gained a draft**". |

Hiding, not deleting: the twelve `x.band.*` knobs keep their registry rows, their mirrored values, the on-page border and the `/replies/generate` gate — they are simply not editable from the panel, because RS.3 left the Sweep gear as the only thing that decides queue admission and two look-alike number sets one tab apart is a trap. Reachable via `PATCH /x/settings` / MCP `x_update_setting` when a ≥100-measured recalibration actually justifies one. **RS.9:** gained `groupResetTarget(rendered, fullCount)` — what a group card's reset button should actually drop: `{kind:'group'}` when the card shows the whole group, `{kind:'keys'}` when a search query has filtered it (never reset a knob the user cannot see — `SettingsGear`'s rule, which the Tuning tab was violating), `null` when nothing in view is overridden so the button is disabled rather than a no-op. Tested in `settingsClient.test.ts`. |
| `src/sidepanel/settingsEditor.ts` | **UI.12 (NEW)** `useSettingsEditor(settings): SettingsEditor` — **the one settings-editing discipline in the panel**, extracted from UI.11's `TuningPanel` so the inline gears could not fork it. Four rules, in one place: optimistic local value → **400 ms debounce per key** (`PATCH_DEBOUNCE_MS`) → **flush (not cancel) on unmount** → on a server refusal record the 400 code per row and re-read `GET /x/settings`. `resetKey` cancels a pending edit instead of flushing it (dropping the override is the newer intent). **RS.8:** the reset primitive is now `resetKeyList(keys)` — **one** `POST /x/settings/reset {keys}` for the whole set (a per-key fan-out would leave a partial reset on the first failure), stamping the failure code on every key it tried; `resetKey(k)` is `resetKeyList([k])`. Returns `{groups,error,rowErrors,busyGroup,change,resetKey,resetKeyList,resetGroupId,reload}`. **One editor per TAB, not per gear** — a second instance holds a second copy of the registry, so a gear edit would leave Tuning stale until reload. |

`system` resolved via `matchMedia`), **UI.6 `settings:server`** (the flat mirrored-knob blob — background-written ONLY; `local`, not `session`, so the content script can read it too and so a cold panel opens on the last known config). **`radar:sightings` + `radar:dismissed` moved OUT of `session` into `local` (2026-07-29 radar-durability fix)** — the session area is dropped on an extension reload/update or a browser-process restart, which silently collapsed a live queue mid-scroll; `readRadar` adopts a legacy session buffer once (both keys absent from `local`) and persists the dismissed list on adoption, `coerceSightings` drops bad ROWS instead of the old all-or-nothing `isRadarSightings` guard (one unreadable row used to read as an empty queue that the next write then persisted), and `pruneStale`/`RADAR_TTL_MS` (24h on `lastSeenAt`, unparseable = keep) is now the only implicit way a row leaves — applied in `readRadar`, in `rehydrateSightings`'s incoming rows (the server keeps drafts `ready` for 48h, so an un-pruned rehydrate would flash day-old rows in on every mount) and in the panel reader. `chrome.storage.session`: `launch:active`, `launch:replies`, **A3.8 `manual:due`** (background-written array of due manual posts, newest-first cap 5; the Today `ManualPostCard` reads it, dismiss/mark-posted route back through the background — single writer §7.24), **AX.6 `stratus:openPerson`** (`{handle, at}` dossier-open handoff — background-written single writer, App.tsx consumes on mount + `onChanged` then clears via `stratus/open-person-clear`). **HS.1** `harvest:handSweep` (the armed hand sweep — `{handle, mode, startedAt, expiresAt}`, 90 min; **written by the panel, removed by either side**) + `harvest:handSweep:stats` (`{startedAt, rows, saved, oldest, runId, updatedAt, error}` — **written by the content script only**, throttled to 1 s, read by the panel; keyed by `startedAt` so a previous sweep's blob is not this sweep's progress). **PP.1 `radar:lastPickAt`** (`local`, epoch ms of the last Radar angle picked — a panel-owned CONTROL like `radar:replyGoal`, written and read by `sidepanel/Radar.tsx` alone; junk/absent/≤0 reads as no pick, which can only under-warn). |
