**The mirrored-settings wire (UI.6, extended UI.7 + UI.12 + UI.14)** — **`x.identity.selfHandle` (OH.1/OH.5 — mirrored because the Harvest tab's "My replies" preset prefills from it; surfaced through `readServerConfig` as `selfHandle`, `SERVER_DEFAULTS` `''`)**, `x.doctrine.anchors3`/`anchors4`/`ladderSwitchAt`, `x.followups.neglectedTargetDays`, the twelve `x.band.*` thresholds, `x.gates.bestTimeMinN`, `x.ai.batchReplyCap`, `x.radar.curatedCount`, `x.mentions.panelRefreshCap`, and the eight `x.display.{doNextCap,doNextSnoozeH,fansAmberTopN,radarDraftCap,dossierListLen,channelPostsShown,voiceListLimit,repliesListLimit}` are the whole `scope:'mirrored'` set (**33 keys** — the number moved 28 → 32 at CQ.1's four `x.cannon.*` and 32 → **33** at OH.1; recount it, never carry it forward — asserted as an exact list in `src/x/settings/registry.test.ts` AND — since UI.14 — as an exact `Object.keys(ServerConfig)` list in `extension/src/shared/serverSettings.test.ts`, so adding one fails on BOTH sides of the wire until both halves land). **UI.12 established the second reason to mirror:** not only "both sides must agree" (band, cadence) but "the panel is the ONLY consumer" — the four display caps have no server reader at all, so `scope:'server'` would make them unreachable by the code that uses them. It also FLIPPED two server keys rather than minting panel twins: `x.followups.neglectedTargetDays` (the Today roster tint must not disagree with the Do-next queue and the digest that read it) and `x.ai.batchReplyCap` (so `radarBatchSize(cfg) = clamp(radarDraftCap, batchReplyCap)` (**RC.4** added its sibling `curatedBatchSize(cfg) = clamp(curatedCount, batchReplyCap)` — the curated pass reads a DIFFERENT pair: `radarDraftCap` has no say, since curation grades the whole queue rather than a display slice) can stop the panel asking for a batch the server refuses — the refusal is not truncation). Note `x.quests.neglectedTargetDays` is a DIFFERENT key in a different group and stays server-only. **Adding a mirrored key is a 2-file move (+2 test edits):** the registry def + a `ServerConfig` field & baked fallback in `extension/src/shared/serverSettings.ts` — a mirrored key with no field is silently never read. **RC.3/RC.4 split that move across two TASKS and proved the failure mode is silent, not loud:** `x.radar.curatedCount` shipped in the registry one task before its `ServerConfig` field, and nothing broke or warned — `readServerConfig` reads NAMED keys and never spreads the blob, so an unmirrored mirrored key is inert rather than corrupting, and the knob simply did nothing on the client for one commit (D179c). If a plan puts the two halves in different tasks, the second one owes `ServerConfig` + `SERVER_DEFAULTS` + `readServerConfig` + BOTH exact-list tests. **UI.14 added the three list caps on exactly this path:** `x.display.dossierListLen` (People's dossier, capping replies/their-mentions/their-saved-tweets — never the timeline), `x.display.channelPostsShown` (the Channels room's pillar posts) and `x.display.voiceListLimit` (the Voice query's page size, `loadTweets`' `limit`, so it is a dependency of that `useCallback`). Consumption follows the server's Decision-6 shape: the pure modules gained a trailing defaulted `cfg` (`pickAnchors(n, cfg)`, `suggestSlotDate(…, cfg)`, `suggestBestSlotDate(…, audience, cfg)`, `buildWeekBoard(…, cfg)`, `slotHint(…, minN)`) so every pre-UI.6 call site and test is byte-identical, and only the COMPONENTS read the blob (via `useServerSettings()`), never the pure modules — the panel mirror of "only routes/workers read the store". `composerLogic` and `calendarLogic` take the SAME config object: the Composer's "Best time" and the Calendar board's ghost anchors must open the same hours or the two surfaces disagree on screen. `x.mentions.serverRefreshCap` is deliberately NOT mirrored — the server cap is the real limit and the panel budget must keep degrading gracefully when the blob is missing. **UI.7 added the CONTENT-SCRIPT half:** `content.ts` resolves the blob itself (module-level `bandThresholds`, `initBandThresholds()` in `start()` = one `chrome.storage.local` read + a `storage.onChanged` listener on area `'local'`, the `initPassiveHarvestSetting` shape) and passes it into every `classifyBand` call — content scripts can't see `session`, which is why the blob lives in `local`. `serverSettings.ts` is no longer literally import-free: it value-imports `BAND` from the `../replyBand.ts` shim, which content.ts already inlines, because BAND is the canonical owner of the twelve defaults on both sides. The rule it lives by is **"nothing that can't be inlined into the IIFE"** (no React, no sidepanel module, nothing with its own deps) — `dist/content.js` having zero `import` statements is the check. **CQ.1** added `ServerConfig.cannon: CannonThresholds` with `SERVER_DEFAULTS.cannon = CANNON` value-imported from the `../cannon.ts` shim — **the four numbers are never re-typed here**, exactly as `BAND` is not; `readServerConfig` guards it per key like the rest. All four `x.cannon.*` knobs ride the mirrored blob, which is what lets `content.ts`'s capture arm and the panel's Cannon view decide with the same floor and cutoff the server does.

**RC.10 reply-craft delta for §5:** `extension/tsconfig.app.json` listed **TEN** out-of-tree shared files at RC.10 (eleven since RS.1 — count the array); the tenth is `extension/src/replyMode.ts` → `../src/shared/replyMode.ts`. It re-exports the canonical ids/angles/table for side-panel rendering and five-angle content/message validation — no extension-local vocabulary.

- `extension/src/shared/types.ts` widens reply variants to the five shared angles, carries per-reply `mode`/`modeSource` on batch results and `curatedMode` on the next request, and mirrors RC.9's Playbook room/opening/capture/contamination shapes.
- `extension/src/shared/messages.ts` + `background.ts` carry resolved mode/source through the batch result into each Radar sighting; `shared/radar.ts::mergeSightings` keeps the old room on a plain re-sight and takes a fresh one on re-draft.
- `extension/src/sidepanel/Radar.tsx` maps curation scores' optional room onto survivors as `curatedMode`, sends it back with the drafting batch, and renders a `room · source` chip on every drafted row before the paste. Angle tabs are whatever the response carries (2/3/1), never a hardcoded trio.
- `extension/src/shared/variantChips.ts`/`.test.ts` and `content.ts` accept/render `observation` and `question`; legacy unknown storage labels remain tolerated at the message boundary rather than deleting a paid draft.
- `extension/src/sidepanel/Playbook.tsx` renders the hard `2026-08-08` angle boundary and new **Room**, **Opening**, **Opening × room**, and **Persona contamination** tables. Capture basis points sit beside yield; old-server tolerance follows the existing three-layer discipline (slice at call site, missing-slice banner, guarded result cell).
- `extension/src/sidepanel/api.ts` needs no new endpoint: the widened shapes ride the existing replies/Playbook calls. `styles.css` adds only the mode-chip presentation; no new semantic colour scale.

**RS radar-manual-first delta for §5 (RS.1–RS.5).** `tsconfig.app.json` `include` is now **eleven** (`../src/shared/radarSweep.ts`); the shim `extension/src/radarSweep.ts` is a bare re-export and therefore sits at the top level, not under `shared/`.

**OU.5 delta for §5 — the TWELFTH out-of-tree shim.** `extension/tsconfig.app.json`'s `include` is now **twelve**: `extension/src/searchQuery.ts` → `src/shared/searchQuery.ts`, the bare 4-line re-export shape (`replyBand.ts`'s), consumed on arrival by `Outliers.tsx`. The inline check is `grep -c 'min_faves' dist/sidepanel.js` (1) plus `-filter:replies` and `x.com/search` — and the counterpart check that it did **not** reach `content.js` (0 on all three): the compiler is side-panel-only, and OU.7 is the task that touches the content script. `extension/src/shared/types.ts` carries the wire shapes (`SavedSearch`/`SavedSearchItem`/`SavedSearchesResponse`/`SavedSearchCapture`/`SavedSearchCreateBody`/`SavedSearchPatchBody`/`SearchDefaultsResponse`/`SearchRunResponse`) and **re-exports `SearchQuery`/`SearchSort`/`CompileResult`/`Problem`/`RepliesFilter`/`MediaFilter` from the shim rather than redeclaring them** (D180a — a hand-mirrored 19-field type drifts from the module doing the work). `api.ts` gains the `searches` namespace (`list`/`defaults`/`get`/`create`/`patch`/`remove`/`run` — no `compile`). `styles.css` gains `.outlier-*` (tokens only, no new colour literal). **No panel unit test: §5's convention, so the suite stayed at 2583/130.**

**RA.1 delta for §5 (no new file, no new shim, no `tsconfig` change).** `extension/src/shared/radar.ts` now *imports* `bandStickiness` + `RadarBandName` from `../radarSweep.ts` (the existing shim) and keeps `export type RadarBand = RadarBandName` as an alias — so every importer, and the on-page capture arm, is untouched, and `extension/dist/content.js` still greps to **0** import statements. `mergeSightings`'s behaviour is byte-for-byte what it was; only the ratchet's home moved (§7.27/D185).

**XR.5 delta for §5 — the THIRTEENTH and FOURTEENTH out-of-tree shims + the Composer's C pill.**
`extension/tsconfig.app.json`'s `include` is now **fifteen entries = fourteen shims** (the first entry is the
extension's own `src/**/*` — count the shims, not the array): `extension/src/xRanker.ts` →
`src/shared/xRanker.ts` and `extension/src/xRankerSignals.ts` → `src/shared/xRankerSignals.ts`, both the bare
re-export shape (`searchQuery.ts`'s). Inline check `grep -c 'rust_home_mixer_favorite_weight'
dist/sidepanel.js` = **1**. Consumers today: `Composer.tsx` (C) and `Radar.tsx` (E, via `sidepanel/radarLogic.ts`); `content.ts` is XR.7's and `grep -c 'rust_home_mixer_favorite_weight' dist/content.js` is still **0**.

- **`Composer.tsx`** — two memos beside the existing coach memo, no new state, no fetch, nothing stored:
  `rankerFeats = rankerDraftFeatures({text: coachInput, hasMediaNote: original?.mediaNote != null,
  isThreadStarter: !isSinglePost})` then `ranker = scoreDraftRanker(coachInput, rankerFeats, {coach})`.
  **Passing `coach` in is the load-bearing part** — it is what stops the two pills from grading two
  evaluations of one draft. Renders as a third element in `.coach-head`: `<span className={rankerBandChip(
  ranker.band) + ' ranker-pill'} title={rankerPillTitle(ranker)}>C {ranker.score} · {rankerPillLabel(ranker)}
  </span>`, plus one `<small className="muted">` under `COACH_DISCLAIMER` saying the two numbers answer
  different questions. Advisory end to end: nothing sorts, gates, disables or reorders on C (§7.23a).
- **`composerLogic.ts`** — `rankerDraftFeatures({text, hasMediaNote, isThreadStarter}) → DraftFeatures`
  (`hasImage` = a Studio visual pinned to the row; `hasExternalLink` = the file's own `URL_RE`, the one the
  cost preview bills on; `isReply`/`isQuote` always false — the Composer drafts originals and threads.
  **`hasVideo`/`videoSeconds`/`isMutualFollow` are ABSENT, never `false`** — §7.11, and asserted with
  `'hasVideo' in f === false`), `rankerPillLabel(r)` (`netNegative` → the word `net-negative`, because
  `offsetScore` squashes and a pill waiting for a `0` never fires — D229) and `rankerPillTitle(r)`
  (head → the signal-free sentence → the net-negative sentence when it applies → `Up:`/`Down:` at most 3
  modifier labels each → the unvalidated-cut-points line → `RANKER_DISCLAIMER` verbatim, never retyped).
- **`styles.css`** — one rule, `.ranker-pill { text-transform: none; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
  align-self: center }`. No colour: the `.chip` family carries it. The transform override is the whole
  reason the rule exists — the family lowercases, and `c 71` reads as a typo.
- **Tests** (§5's "panel components are untested by convention" still holds — what is tested is the pure
  half): `composerLogic.test.ts` +13, `CoachChip.test.ts` +3 (the ranker-tone describe lives there because
  the claim is about the COACH's vocabulary not leaking, even though the function is in `chips.ts`).

**XR.6 delta for §5 — the E chip on Radar sightings (one NEW file pair, no new shim, no `tsconfig` change,
no CSS).**

- **`extension/src/sidepanel/radarLogic.ts` (NEW, pure)** — `sightingCounts(s) → MeasuredCounts`
  (`likes: s.likes ?? null` — RS.2 stamps it only when the sweep read one; `replies: s.signals.replies`, where
  `0` IS a reading because X renders no count at zero; **`reposts: null` — a sighting has no repost field and
  neither does `radar_sightings`**, §7.11), `sightingRankerScore(s)` (= `scoreMeasured(counts)` with **no**
  `DraftFeatures`), `rankerChipFace(r)` (`E 52 · strong shape`) and `rankerChipTitle(r)`.
  **Sidepanel-local, not `shared/radar.ts`, and the reason is the bundle:** `content.ts` imports
  `shared/radar.ts`, so a ranker import there would pull X's weight table into the content script — the
  bundle XR.7 owns, whose inline proof is `grep -c 'rust_home_mixer_favorite_weight' dist/content.js` = **0**
  before it and 1 after. `composerLogic.ts` is the precedent (D239).
  **No features are passed, deliberately** (D240): the only one `scoreMeasured` reads is the mutual-follow
  reply boost, and the nearest thing a sighting carries is `personTier` — our own CRM stage, not an X follow
  edge. Every row is scored on the base reply weight, which is the weight the E baseline is pinned at (D231),
  so numerator and denominator stay on the same terms and two rows of one queue compare.
- **`Radar.tsx`** — one `useMemo(() => sightingRankerScore(s), [s])` per row and one `<span>` in
  `.radar-row-head`, between the band chip and `.radar-author`: everything past `.radar-author` (`flex: 1`)
  describes the REPLY, this describes the tweet. `className={rankerBandChip(ranker.band) + ' ranker-pill'}` —
  **XR.5's exact construction, and `.ranker-pill` is reused rather than re-cut**, so no CSS moved. Gated on
  `ranker.available`: a row whose views were never captured renders **no chip**, never `E 0` (which reads as
  "this post is dead" instead of "we didn't look"). Read-only against the buffer — nothing is stamped onto
  the sighting, so `mergeSightings` needs no rule for a value that is always re-derivable (§7.24).
- **The tooltip's head line is DERIVED from `r.contributions`, not quoted from `scoreMeasured`'s own
  `note`** — that sentence names all three observable heads, which is true of a harvest row and false of a
  sighting. `r.note` is reused verbatim only on the `lowSample` branch, where it says the right thing.
  Then the Decision-9 caveat (the chip is on the POST because `OONRetweetReplyFilter` drops an
  out-of-network reply from For You outright), the quartile line, and `RANKER_DISCLAIMER`.

**RA.2 delta for §5 (one NEW file, no new shim, no `tsconfig` change — `radarIngest.ts` is an ordinary
`shared/` module, not an out-of-tree re-export).**

- **`extension/src/shared/radarIngest.ts` (NEW, pure)** — `RADAR_SYNC_KEY` (`'radarSightingSync'`),
  `RADAR_INGEST_BATCH_MAX` (100), `RADAR_INGEST_RESEND_MS` (60 s), `SIGHTING_MAX_AGE_MIN`/`SIGHTING_PATH_MAX`,
  `shouldShipSighting(sent, band, nowMs, resendMs?)` (never-sent → true, band changed → true, else the
  window), `toSightingWireRow(s, sourcePath): SightingWireInput | null` and `pathFromTabUrl(url)`. The
  `shared/passiveHarvest.ts` twin, one feed over; `SightingWireInput` hand-mirrors the server's
  `SightingWireRow` (build isolation) the way `shared/types.ts` mirrors the settings JSON.
- **`background.ts`** — `radarSyncEnabled` + `initRadarSyncSetting()` (the `content.ts::initPassiveHarvestSetting`
  shape: one `chrome.storage.local` read + an `onChanged` listener on area `local`, absent ⇒ enabled),
  a module-level `sightingSentAt` throttle map (cleared past 3,000 entries, and torn down with the MV3
  worker anyway), and `shipSightings(sightings, sourcePath)` — fire-and-forget in the `markDraftsOnServer`
  idiom, ≤100 rows, remainder deliberately left unmarked so it ships on the next report. Called from the
  **`isRadarReport` branch's success arm, after `sendResponse`**; `sourcePath` is read off `sender.tab?.url`
  BEFORE the buffer write (the tab can navigate while it is in flight), which is the whole reason the hook
  lives here and not in `content.ts::flushRadar`.
- **`sidepanel/storage.ts` + `Settings.tsx`** — `Settings.radarSightingSync` (10th field, default `true`)
  through `getSettings`/`saveSettings`/`patchSettings` **and `useSettings`'s `onChanged` key filter** (the
  HV.3 missed-key lesson), plus the fifth `.voice-toggle` row under the passive-harvest one. **Three
  `Settings` object literals exist outside storage.ts** — `Settings.tsx`'s `currentSettings` memo (deps
  array too) and its `onSave` `next`, and `sidepanel/storage.test.ts`'s round-trip blob — and typecheck
  catches all three.

- **`content.ts` — the behaviour change lives here.** *(Superseded in part: the classifier is gone, `applyBand` is now `applyCapture`, and the `data-stratus-band` border/dim half described below no longer exists.)* It keeps `readTweetCapture` and its `recordPassiveHarvest(article)` tail; **every `recordRadarSighting` call sits inside `if (cap && sig && sweepIsArmed())`** — false for an absent `radar:sweep` key, which is the default state. Arms, in gate order: `passesSweep(cand, sweepCfg)` → `'sweep'`; else `cfg.campedBypass && isCampedSighting(...)` → `'cannon'`; else `cfg.circleBypass && isRosterSighting(...)` → `'roster'`. **The border write and the passive-harvest tail are deliberately OUTSIDE that block and each carries a comment saying so** — this is the first thing a later reader will "tidy up", and gating the harvest would make `buildTimelineFunnel` measure button presses instead of the timeline. `initBandThresholds` became **`initMirroredConfig`** (one `readServerConfig` read + one listener resolving `band` + `sweep`; **`cannonCfg` is GONE — nothing on the page reads `x.cannon.*` any more**), `initSweepState()` holds the session behind `sweepIsArmed()` which re-resolves through `sweepActiveAt(…, Date.now())` on **every** call (no timer), `readTweetCapture(article)` is the ONE aria parse (`readTweetSignals` is a two-line wrapper over it, so every existing caller is byte-equivalent) and now also yields `likes`, `isCannonSighting` → **`isCampedSighting`** (age bound from `sweepCfg.maxAgeMin`; the `isCannonEligible` score path deleted), `ROSTER_MAX_AGE_MIN` **deleted** (one age rule for every arm), and `recordRadarSighting` takes an extras arg carrying `likes`/`verified` (`verified?: boolean | null`, with `null` OMITTED — `RadarSighting.verified` is `boolean` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and "unread badge" is not a claim either way). **RS.5 added two page affordances:** `syncSweepChip()` from `scan()` and from the `SWEEP_STATE_KEY` `onChanged` listener (one `div.stratus-sweep-chip` portalled to `<body>`, fixed bottom-left, live countdown through `sweepMinutesLeft`, click → `remove` the key, one `setTimeout` at `expiresAt + 250ms` so a quiet page still clears it, and a **failed stop re-renders "still sweeping" rather than vanishing**), and `syncRadarAddStates()` over a module-level `queuedIds` mirror fed by one `chrome.storage.local.get(RADAR_SIGHTINGS_KEY)` + an `onChanged` listener — **read-only in both directions (§7.24), pruned at read time with the panel's own `pruneStale`** so the ⊕ never lights a row the panel has aged out. The tweetId is **re-derived per scan, never cached on the button** (X recycles action rows as it virtualises, so a remembered id eventually lights the ⊕ on somebody else's post); a `data-sig` skip means an unchanged scan writes no DOM, and the 1.5 s post-click revert clears `data-state` **and** `data-sig` because `syncRadarAddStates` skips buttons reading `added`.
- **`shared/verified.ts` (NEW) + its happy-dom suite** — the DOM half: `readVerified(article): boolean | null`, scoped to the **FIRST `User-Name` block** rather than composed against the whole article (a descendant selector would let a **quoted tweet's** verified author vouch for the outer post — two fixtures pin both directions). Ordered selector list, structural not textual: `svg[data-testid="icon-verified"]` first, then `svg[aria-label*="erified" i]`. `null` = the name block itself was absent. **The aria fallback covers case, not language** — a Romanian "Cont verificat" reads `false`, pinned by a test rather than hidden, because under `verifiedOnly` a refusal is the direction this filter is built to fail in. `[data-testid="icon-verified"]` is the load-bearing selector and the first place to look if a `verifiedOnly` scroll admits nothing at all.
- **`shared/tweetKind.ts` (NEW, SW.1) + its happy-dom suite (17 tests)** — the DOM half of the sweep's two CONTENT gates, `verified.ts`'s sibling down to the header discipline (dependency-free so it inlines into the content IIFE; every structural assumption a named exported constant so a drift is one edit). `readHasMedia(article)` scans `MEDIA_SELECTORS` (`tweetPhoto`, `videoPlayer`, `videoComponent`, `previewInterstitial`) and skips any hit whose `closest('[data-testid^="card."]')` matches — a link unfurl's thumbnail is not the author's photo — while a **quoted tweet's** photo deliberately DOES count (the opposite call from `readVerified`'s quote scoping, and for a stated reason: the cell in front of you does show an image). `readPromoted(article)` is structural first (`placementTracking`), then an English-only `socialContext` text arm: `PROMOTED_TEXT_PREFIXES = ['promoted','sponsored']` plus `PROMOTED_TEXT_EXACT = ['ad']`, exact so **"Adam liked" is not an ad** — the one false positive this reader cannot afford, because it silently drops a real tweet with nothing on screen saying why. **Neither returns `null`:** absence is a complete answer here, unlike a missing name block.
- **`shared/radar.ts`** — *(Superseded: `RadarBand` is now exactly `'manual'|'roster'|'cannon'|'sweep'` — every value a capture REASON, no verdicts left. `bandWeight` and its `rankSightings` rung are deleted [with only reasons left there was nothing to order], and `coerceSightings` folds legacy `'hot'`/`'warm'` session rows onto `'sweep'` so an extension upgrade cannot empty a live queue.)* `RadarBand` += `'sweep'` (stickiness **1**, the sweep/cannon rung), `isRadarSighting` accepts it, and `RadarSighting` gained `likes?`/`verified?`, merged in `mergeSightings` on the same terms as `reply`/`draftId` (incoming wins, a metric-less re-sighting keeps what an earlier one captured). **These two fields are extension-only** — not on the batch wire, no column, and deliberately NOT added to `TweetSignals` (that type is stored inside `radar_drafts.signals`/`reply_drafts.contextSnapshot` and read by the band gate and the timeline funnel). `RADAR_TTL_MS`'s comment was stale on arrival — it justified 24h as "the same 24h `ROSTER_MAX_AGE_MIN` uses", and that constant is deleted here; rewritten to stand on its own.
- **`shared/serverSettings.ts`** — `ServerConfig.sweep: SweepConfig`, `SERVER_DEFAULTS.sweep = SWEEP` (imported through the shim, the `CANNON` pattern), `readSweep(blob)` with the same **per-key** fallback discipline as `readBand`/`readCannon`, plus the new `readBoolean` helper (the mirror's first boolean keys). **SW.1** added `readMediaFilter` — the mirror's first ENUM key, membership-tested (`'any'|'with'|'without'`) so a blob carrying an option this build never heard of falls back to baked rather than reaching `passesContentGates` as a string that matches neither branch and silently disables the gate.
- **`sidepanel/Radar.tsx` + `styles.css`** — a `.radar-sweep` row under the tab strip in **all three views** (a sweep is global, unlike the queue-only humanize label): Start/Stop, the three-shape state line, and a **second `SettingsGear`** over `SWEEP_KEYS` fed by the section's **existing** `useSettingsEditor` (one editor per tab — a second would be a second registry copy). `sweeping` is `sweepActiveAt(raw, Date.now()) !== null` **resolved on every render, never held in state**; the 1 s interval only bumps a tick counter. Both writes are optimistic with a real rollback — **a failed stop puts the row back to `Sweeping`**, because the page really is still capturing. The ended notice is suppressed for a stop the user pressed (only an expiry the panel *watched* produces it) and the stale key is deliberately left in storage rather than cleaned up on mount. `.radar-sweep-btn.armed` is `--strat-ok`, not `--strat-accent` (it sits one row under the accent-tinted `.radar-tab.active`, and "a thing is running" must not read as "a tab is selected"); the ended state is `--strat-warn`, not `--strat-danger`. `.radar-band-sweep` is muted like `.radar-band-roster` but **dashed** — the rule that admitted the row is one the user can change. **The Queue empty state is now two states** (manual-and-empty = the default state of a working install; sweeping-and-empty = the sentence that sends you to the ⚙, and the one that surfaces a drifted `readVerified` under `verifiedOnly`); never collapse them back into one line.

**RQ ingest-and-consume delta for §5 (2026-08-11, RQ.1 — one commit, no plan file; extension-only + one server comment).** The reported bug: tweets that cleared every sweep filter never reached the queue. Two independent ceilings did it, and both are gone.

- **SP.1 — named sweep presets (`sidepanel/SweepPresets.tsx` NEW + `ui/GearPopover.tsx` + `SettingsGear.tsx` + `settingsClient.ts` + `shared/types.ts` + `styles.css`).** `GearPopover`/`SettingsGear` gained an optional **`head`** slot rendered between the note and the rows; the sweep gear fills it with `<SweepPresets>`, which sits **above the rows a Load overwrites** (cause above effect). Three things a later session needs. **(1) Only a NAME ever leaves the panel** — save snapshots server-side, load writes back server-side, so the panel holds no copy of the eleven numbers and there is no second place they can be wrong. **(2) A load calls `requestSettingsSync()` (newly EXPORTED from `settingsClient.ts`) as well as `editor.reload()`** — the eleven keys are `mirrored` and the load went through `/x/sweep/presets/load` rather than `patchSetting`, so nothing else would tell the background to re-pull, and the content script would keep sweeping on the OLD filters until the blob's TTL. This is the one failure mode the feature can have that the panel cannot see. **(3) `reload`, never the optimistic path** — `useSettingsEditor`'s optimism exists to track a slider drag; a load moves eleven rows at once and the values that landed are the server's. `SweepPresetsResponse`/`SweepPresetLoadResponse`/`SweepPreset` live in `shared/types.ts` with `values: SweepConfig` **re-exported from the `../radarSweep.ts` shim**, never hand-mirrored (the `HumanizerConfig` precedent). `api.sweepPresets.{list,save,load,remove}` sits beside `humanizer`, not inside `settings`.
- **NW.1 — the `Reach | Network` switch (`sidepanel/Radar.tsx` + `shared/radar.ts` + `styles.css`).** A `.radar-goal` segmented control immediately LEFT of the two spending buttons (hidden in Clicked, like `Draft replies`, because nothing there spends), disabled while either button is in flight. Panel state persisted at **`REPLY_GOAL_KEY = 'radar:replyGoal'`** in `chrome.storage.local` — a CONTROL, not part of the sightings buffer, so §7.24's single-writer rule doesn't apply (the `passiveCapture` precedent); any unrecognized value reads as `reach`. It is deliberately NOT a server setting: a server setting would silently apply the objective to the MCP tools and the CLI too. `sendBatch` sends `goal` on EVERY batch, so **both** buttons honour it (Curate & draft grades the queue exactly as before, then drafts the survivors for whichever goal is set), and `goalNote(out)` appends ` · networking` to the note from the SERVER's echo — silent on `reach`, the same rule `languageNote` keeps for English.
- **`shared/radar.ts` — the two caps split into three constants.** `RADAR_CAP` **100 → 500**: it was a policy dressed as a buffer size, and an armed 30-minute sweep on a busy timeline admits more than 100 tweets, so the surplus was evicted before the human ever saw it. **`CURATE_REQUEST_CAP` (NEW, 100)** is what `Radar.tsx` clamps a curate call to — the two used to be one constant "by construction", and the route REFUSES an over-long batch rather than truncating it, so conflating them again 400s the whole pass (`MAX_CURATE_TWEETS`'s doc comment in `src/x/replies/curate.ts` was rewritten to say the same thing from the other side; a test in `radar.test.ts` pins the pair). **The dismissed set is now `Tombstone {id, at}[]`, not `string[]`** — it was a permanent blocklist bounded only by how much you dismissed, which is the second ceiling: `RADAR_DISMISSED_TTL_MS` (24h = `RADAR_TTL_MS`, past which a sweep can't re-admit the tweet anyway) with the cap raised to 5000 as pure storage bounding. `coerceDismissed(v, nowMs)` owns the read, the TTL and the **legacy `string[]` migration** (stamped `nowMs` — one extra window of blocking, the safe direction); `appendDismissed(d, ids, nowMs)` re-stamps on re-dismiss; `purgeDismissed`/`dismissedIds` are the other two. **`mergeSightings` has exactly one tombstone exception: `band === 'manual'`** — a ⊕ pin on something you dismissed is a person changing their mind, and it used to be answered with silence. **Eviction moved off `bandStickiness` onto `evictionWeight`** (manual 3 > has `reply`/`clickedAt` 2 > sweep/cannon 1 > roster 0): a paid draft outranks an unworked capture, which the old shared rung got backwards.
- **`background.ts`** — `readRadar` returns `Tombstone[]` through `coerceDismissed`; `addSightings` calls `purgeDismissed` for incoming `manual` ids and **writes the dismissed key only when a pin actually resurrected something**, so an ordinary sweep flush stays a one-key write. `markDraftsOnServer` now **chunks at `MAX_DRAFT_PATCH_IDS` (200, restated from `routes/radar.ts`)** — one click can dismiss 500 rows and an unchunked PATCH would 400 the lot, leaving every server row `ready` to resurrect at the next rehydrate.
- **`sidepanel/Radar.tsx` — a drafting pass CONSUMES the queue** (the user's rule, chosen explicitly over "clear only what was sent"): `consumeQueue(pass, draftedIds)` dismisses every row the pass covered that came back without a reply — model skips, rows past the batch cap that were never sent, **⊕ pins included**. `sendBatch` returns `draftedIds` for it (a count can't say *which* two of twenty are missing). `passSet` is the view's whole undrafted set (`fresh`, or the cannon rows in the Cannon view — a filtered view must not clear rows it isn't showing) and the curated path snapshots `pass = fresh` **before the first await**, or a sweep still running underneath loses rows the pass never covered. **A whole-call failure clears nothing** and the note ends `· queue kept` / `· rest of the queue kept`: a dead call is not a verdict on any tweet, and it is the one unrecoverable failure on this surface. Curated drops are excluded from the consume count so the note doesn't claim them twice.

## 6. MCP + integrations

- `POST /mcp` — 28 X tools (see §3.3 `x/mcp.ts`; **TH.2** added `x_threads` + `x_thread`, both `route('/x/harvest/threads…')`; **RA.3** added `x_radar` + `x_radar_tweet`, both `route('/x/radar/sightings…')`; **RA.4** added write-tier `x_radar_draft_reply` → `POST /x/radar/drafts/compose`; **RQ.3** gave `x_radar` a `queue?: boolean` input (→ `queue=true`, described as the live panel queue: seen in the last 24 h, not dismissed, not worked) — **a new input key, not a new tool, so the count holds**; all five $0, and the exact count is asserted by `src/mcp.test.ts` + four count strings in `docs/s2-mcp-server.md` — the prose total, the `## The tools` line, the `### <tier> (N)` heading of the tier you touched, and the end-to-end verification line). Client setup: `claude mcp add --transport http stratus https://<host>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $STRATUS_TOKEN"`.
- `.claude/skills/stratus` — drives the HTTP API from Claude Code (scheduling scripts `md_to_schedule.ts`; always jitter minutes). **UI.6:** the ladder is no longer hand-synced — `loadAnchors()` GETs `/x/settings/values?scope=mirrored` (env `STRATUS_API_TOKEN ?? API_TOKEN`, base `STRATUS_BASE_URL`, 5 s timeout, the api.sh convention) and uses `x.doctrine.anchors3`/`anchors4`. Every failure — no token, dead host, non-2xx, malformed body, or a configured ladder whose length ≠ slots/day — silently keeps the baked `[9,13,18]`/`[8,12,16,20]`, and the stderr summary names which source won. A settings read must never fail a scheduling run.
- `.claude/skills/radar-analyst` — **RA.7**, the analysis + drafting protocol over the three RA tools (`SKILL.md` + `references/queries.md` + `references/reply-craft.md`). **Documentation only, no source, no test** — its correctness is that it never names a tool/route/column that does not exist, so a task that renames one owes this skill in the same commit (the `docs/*.md` quoted-string rule, extended to `.claude/skills/`). Its nine `x_query` recipes were each run through `runSelect()` against a freshly migrated `:memory:` DB at authoring time — repeat that check rather than eyeballing column names. **The operating model was narrowed by the operator on 2026-08-18 and this bullet supersedes the ladder narrated in the header stamp:** a pass reads `x_radar` (the whole input) + `x_niche` (once, for the minority of posts whose room licenses the persona) and drafts from the sighting row alone — `x_playbook`, `x_person`, `x_me`, `x_query` and even `x_radar_tweet` are **on-request only**, not steps, because the list already carries `drafted`/`replied` and the `stage`/`isTarget` join. Selection is a four-stage funnel built for a 60–100 row queue when the operator names a size ("the best 25"): drop (worked / aged out vs the echoed `sweep.maxAgeMin` / `bait` / unanswerable-from-text), rank on `vpm` + **`views/(replies+1)` room-to-be-seen** + freshness with relationship and intent-band boosts, an answerability pass over ~1.4x the ask, then a 2-per-handle spread cap and an aggregate cut report. **`references/reply-craft.md` is the drafting prompt this path does not otherwise have** — `x_radar_draft_reply` takes a string and a label, so the room/register call, the persona level (`off` by default), the language rules and the whole anti-LLM style discipline are the session's job. It **mirrors** `REPLY_MODES`/`PersonaUse`/`REPLY_ANGLES` from `src/shared/replyMode.ts` and `LANGUAGE_PROFILES` from `src/shared/language.ts`, and lifts prose from `reply prompt.md` + `src/x/replies/networkPrompt.ts`; **nothing asserts that mirror** (unlike the byte-sync tests on the TS prompt literals), so a task that retunes the mode table, the angle union or a language profile owes this file too, and the file itself says the source wins on a disagreement. One deliberate divergence from `/x/replies/generate`: the route hard-codes ONE `extends` variant for any resolved language, the skill ships the room's full angle set for English and Romanian (the operator reads both) and one variant plus a literal gloss for a language they do not.

## 7. Patterns & conventions (name these in plans; point implementers at the exemplar file)

**Money/API discipline**
1. **One place to call X / Grok / images**: `xFetch` / `askGrok` / `generateImages`. Never raw fetch.
2. **Retire-before-snapshot** (historical — the pattern's only user, `dailyMetrics`, was deleted 2026-08-12): a billed read must be unrepeatable — take the row out of the candidate set in a committed txn BEFORE the read/write that follows. At-most-once, never double-charge. Still the rule the day a read is ever added back; today it is unenforceable-by-absence (invariant #8).
3. **Claim-before-call** (publisher, winner re-read): commit the state flip before the irreversible external call.
4. **Refuse-before-spend**: validation → grounding checks → THEN the paid call (**the band gate that used to sit second is gone with its classifier; body/language/mode validation is now the whole pre-spend ladder on `/replies/generate`**) (replies.ts, icebreakers.ts, images.ts hard budget).
4a. **A money-gate carve-out is server-decided, measured, and stamped** (GT.6). *(Both instances — GT.6 `roster` and CQ.3 `cannon` — are DELETED at RS.10 along with the band gate they carved out of. The principle stands for the next money gate; there is no live carve-out in the tree today.)* the exemption is computed from OUR data on the gate's REFUSAL arm only (a passing call never pays the lookup), never read from the request (§7.16 — a client-sent exemption weakens the gate for every caller), and it writes a marker into the persisted snapshot (`contextSnapshot.gateBypass`) so the exempt calls stay a cohort you can measure instead of an invisible hole. Size the membership rule against the real corpus BEFORE shipping it (§7.33): a carve-out that covers almost every call is not a carve-out, it is the gate turned off, and the marker it stamps is a constant (the D154a/D156a failure). **SECOND INSTANCE (CQ.3), and it is what the rule looks like when it is followed twice:** `isCannonHandleSafe` sits directly beside `isReciprocityHandleSafe` on the same refusal arm, and it stamps **`gateBypass = 'cannon'`, deliberately a different string from `'roster'`** — two carve-outs sharing one marker would put both cohorts in the same SQL bucket and undo the reason the marker exists. The sizing check is in the code rather than in a plan: the roster is a hand-curated 15–25 handles, so this carve-out is structurally small, and the comment says that if `GET /x/cannon/targets` ever returns hundreds the carve-out has become the gate turned off. Note also what CQ *refused* to do — the obvious cheap move was to widen `targetBandMinX/MaxX` past 10 so big accounts cleared the existing carve-out; reading the code first showed `classifyBand` is size-agnostic (those knobs gate no reply at all, they feed `loadTargetHandles()`), so widening would have unblocked nothing while turning a carve-out measured at 14 handles into "every large account I ever saved". **A new membership set is the cheap thing; widening an existing doctrine knob to reach a new cohort is the expensive one.**
4b. **Reusing one membership set for a GATE and for a MEASUREMENT needs a time qualifier, not a second set** (GT.7): the gate asks "is this person mine *now*", which is right at decision time — but a counter over the same set asks "was this act reciprocal", and if the act is what *creates* the membership (`RECIPROCITY_MIN_STAGE = engaged` = "I have replied to them") the counter grades its own input and degenerates into a copy of the volume metric it was meant to contrast. Add an `{asOf}` scope to the ONE loader (the stage half requires a rung stamped before the cutoff — `stageUpdatedAt` is written only on an actual rung change, so it means "when they became this"; a curated half like the roster is never scoped) rather than minting a second rule that can drift. **Test for it the same way §7.33 says: replay the real corpus. Here every one of 14 posted replies was a first contact, so the unqualified count would have equalled the replies quest on every day in history.**
4c. **When a client has to re-decide a server membership rule, reproduce the RULE — never a proxy that happens to be nearby** (GT.8): the content IIFE cannot import the server module (db + drizzle), so the floor is duplicated in a pure `shared/` predicate with reciprocal twin comments (the D151e ladder discipline). The trap is the cached map you already have: `GET /people/glance` is a **superset** of the gate's set, and "the author is in the map" reads like membership while actually meaning *anyone stratus has ever seen* — measured 1,596 vs 14 on prod, a 114× wider rule wearing the same words. Narrow the superset with the real predicate, then **prove the two sides agree on real data** (fetch both endpoints, diff the key sets — $0, one round-trip, no deploy) rather than reasoning that they must. A client/server fork over a shared threshold is the UI.7 badge-vs-gate failure, and it is silent: both sides look right in isolation. **The CQ.4 counter-example is worth knowing, because it tells you when this rule does NOT apply:** `isCannonPerson(entry) = entry?.isCannon === true` reproduces nothing — `isCannon` is the server's own answer, filled by `GET /people/glance` from `loadCannonHandles()` and carried over the wire, so there is no superset to narrow and no rule to fork. The twin comments say *that* explicitly, so nobody later "hardens" it into a stage/target predicate and reintroduces the very fork this section exists to prevent. Carrying the answer beats reproducing the rule whenever the client can get it for free on a request it was already making.
5. **`max_results` clamps** on every paginate wrapper (endpoints.ts pattern).
6. **costHint** when the URL can't price itself; `console.warn` on $0-priced billed calls.

**Data discipline**
7. **Deterministic event ids** `type:ref_table:ref_id` + INSERT OR IGNORE — backfill, live hooks, and DOM ingest share one idempotent id space (people/store.ts, launch.ts). **Bounded-re-log variant (sightings.ts, NT.2 engagements.ts):** when no ref resolves, bucket the id by UTC day (`…:<YYYY-MM-DD>`) instead of falling back to a random uuid — a re-scroll then collapses into one event/day/handle/kind rather than flooding the timeline. A once-ever fact (a follow) drops the date too.
8. **Best-effort side writes**: `safeLogPersonEvents`, `persistRadarDrafts`, `consumeIdeaSafe` — a hook failure never fails the paying path.
9. **Fill-only vs overwrite upserts**: hover/launch glimpses fill-only; profile scrapes overwrite (people/store.ts).
10. **Status ratchets**: stages only auto-promote; radar drafts ready→clicked→expired; mentions never regress implicitly.
11. **null = unknown, never "no"** (`has_media`, `pinned_tweet_id`); bucket null separately in aggregations.
12. **No derived-state tables** when a read-time regroup works (conversations C2, momentum C5).
13. **Sync SQLite**: txns take sync callbacks (`.all()/.get()/.run()`, no await inside); never bind a JS `Date` in raw `sql` (use `.getTime()`); token refresh critical section = in-process mutex.
13a. **Millisecond ties break ordering logic**: writes are sub-millisecond here, so any column an ordering/recency rule reads (`created_at` insertion order, `last_used_at` anti-repeat) must be stamped **monotonically past the row set's current max**, not from `Date.now()` alone. Exemplars both in `replyLists.ts`: items `createdAt` (RL.2), `/use` `lastUsedAt` (RL.3 — measured: 241/500 uses shared a millisecond and 4 immediate repeats slipped through without it).
- **API checkpoint columns are never written from the page (C7 launch.ts, C10 notifications)**: `mentions`'s max tweet_id IS the since_id checkpoint, so a DOM-scraped id would skip every unseen mention — page surfaces READ mention rows for context and route their own writes into `person_events` instead; freshness gaps close via a human-clicked capped refresh, never an auto-pull.

- **Ambient ingest = free-text discriminator + server-owned parent row + lazy prune (HV.1 `POST /harvest/passive`)**: a high-volume DOM feed reuses the existing table instead of forking one — discriminated by a `mode` value the client-facing create route still rejects, hung off one server-found-or-created per-UTC-day run, retention pruned on the ingest path rather than by a new worker (§7.12 spirit). Before opening the tap, check that **every existing reader already filters on that discriminator**. **The client half (HV.2)** is the flushSightings transport with one extra rule: the ambient flush is **warn-and-drop, never retried** (a lost sighting is a missing point on a curve, not a lost user action), its resend throttle mirrors the server's recapture window so the wire carries no row the server would only skip, and the expensive DOM read sits BEHIND the throttle check — a scan-loop hook runs on every mutation burst, so gate order is the performance contract.

**Prompt discipline**
14. **Byte-sync prompts**: `.md` ↔ TS literal asserted by test; regenerate the literal when editing the .md.
15. **Variable tail**: ALL per-call content ({{TWEET_CONTEXT}}, {{PILLARS}}, relationship, guidance, idea) after the stable cacheable instruction prefix; `prompt_cache_key` set.
16. **Server-stamped fields**: `relationship`/`guidance`/gate signals are stamped server-side, never parsed from clients; persist exactly what the model saw in `contextSnapshot`. **OU.7 states the general shape of it: the client reports an OBSERVATION, the server decides the MEANING.** The scrape body carries `sourcePath` (a raw `location.pathname`) and never a `source`; `routes/voice.ts::scrapeSourceFor` maps it to the stored vocabulary. So a new provenance value is a server edit rather than a content-script release (the page can't be re-deployed to every open tab anyway), a compromised or stale page cannot name its own provenance, and `outlier_search` appears **nowhere** in the extension bundle. Same reading of RQ.1's `dismissed_at` (stamped from the server clock, never taken from the wire) and RA.4's band/signals (rebuilt from the stored sighting, never the caller).
17. **Structured outputs** via `text.format` json_schema on `/v1/responses` (`response_format` 400s there).
18. **No fabrication**: Grok may narrate only supplied FACTS; grounding blocks travel back in responses.
- **Provenance in grounding (JD.1, study §G2/§G5)**: two rules that ride on rendered VALUES, never on templates — so neither can move a byte-synced literal. (a) **Machine output must not re-enter "your voice."** Any few-shot block selecting from own measured posts caps drafter-authored rows at a minority (`topWinners`: `MACHINE_WINNERS_MAX = 2` of 5, provenance via `scheduled_posts.source` through `posted_tweet_id`; `posts_published.source` is the publish path, not authorship). Dilution, not exclusion — a hand-edited machine draft is partly the user's. The same exposure exists on the reply side (`reply_drafts.source` → `topAngles` guidance) and is **not yet fixed**. (b) **Scraped text is labelled where it lands**: `UNTRUSTED_CONTEXT_MARKER` heads the rendered tweet-context / posts value in `replies/prompt.ts`, exactly once per render, scoped so it never contradicts the server-stamped instruction blocks at the tail.
- **Niche persona substitution (N.3/N.4)**: `{{PERSONA}}`/`{{BELIEFS}}` (post) and `{{REPLY_PERSONA}}` (reply, single + batch) substitute IN PLACE (deliberate §7.15 deviation — constant per niche ⇒ prefix byte-stable per niche); all niche fields are server-stamped from `loadActiveNicheSafe()` (never client-parsed) and cache keys carry `:slug:updatedAtMs` to bust on edits. The reply routes also stamp `contextSnapshot.niche={slug}` (single path only — batch has no DB row) and load the niche AFTER the band gate. Seed-niche output is bit-for-bit identical to pre-extraction (equivalence tests in `src/test.test.ts` with independent fixtures — never re-read the .md, it holds the tokens now). **N.5 (doctrine):** the 5 REPLY-GUIDE knobs (reply target min/max, week reply %, target band min/max ×) are owned by `niches.doctrine`; consumers call `loadDoctrine()` (never throws, resolves over `DEFAULT_DOCTRINE`) — `targetBand`'s new 2nd arg defaults to `{minX:2,maxX:10}` so untouched call sites/tests stay green (regression), and null doctrine = today's numbers. Doctrine is method-configuration, NOT a stat — no gates touched (§7.19). **N.6 (ownership):** `content_pillars.niche` + `channels.niche` (nullable, backfilled `builder`) make pillars/channels owned by a niche; all list/active reads scope by `ownedByNiche(activeSlug)` = `niche = active.slug OR niche IS NULL` (legacy tolerance — identity until a 2nd niche exists), POSTs stamp the active slug, the channel `:slug` room 404s cross-niche, and `getActivePillars()` returns `[]` for a non-`builder` niche with no pillars → the drafter refuses `409 no_pillars_for_niche` before any Grok spend (zero builder-pillar leakage into another niche's drafts). Last-active pillar 409 is now per-niche. PATCH/DELETE stay slug-addressed (admin can still edit another niche's rows). **AI.3 (prompt registry):** editable prompts live as OVERRIDE ROWS in `prompt_overrides` — row absent = shipped default, restore = DELETE, `customized` is structural row-presence (never a diff). Call sites load `loadPromptSafe(key)` and thread the body into the builders (`buildGrokInput` opts `template?` / `BuildPostDraftOptions.template?`; a per-request `systemPromptOverride` beats the DB override — explicit > DB > code-default); cache keys = registry sha-8 + the niche `:slug:updatedAtMs` suffix (both dimensions vary the rendered prefix). `validatePromptBody` guards edits: `required` placeholders must survive, the niche persona placeholders are `optional` (token-tolerant — an override hardcoding its persona is sanctioned, D29d), unknown tokens warn. A new editable prompt = one `PROMPT_SPECS` entry + a call-site wire (AI.4 adds the editor routes; AI.5/AI.6 migrated the 7 existing prompts, AI.7/AI.8/AI.9 added the three new-surface prompts thread/rewrite/ideas, RL.4 appended `reply-list` — **11 keys**). Registry defaults MUST come from PURE modules — a route-file import cycles (AI.5's `voice/extractPrompt.ts` move exists for exactly that; digest.ts/icebreakers.ts were already pure enough). (Unnumbered — the numbered `§7.N` refs are load-bearing; don't renumber.)

**Stats discipline**
19. **Gates**: playbook cells + all lifts n≥20/side (`DEFAULT_MIN_CELL_N`, **HV.5**: the timeline funnel gates on its `seen` DENOMINATOR, not on measured outcomes — `rate` null below it); angle preference ≥3 measured; best-times top n≥3; BAND recalibration ≥100 and manual-only. Below gate → `sufficient:false`/null, never a confident number.

**Routing/wiring traps**
20. **Static path before `:param`** (followups+fans and rankmap before `/people/:handle`) — check on every new people-adjacent route.
21. **Public-by-design routes** (`/healthz`, `/explorer`) mount at root outside the `/x/*` guard.
22. **LLM-gated mount vs runtime 503** (AI.6 — was Grok-gated): user-facing-always routes mount always + check `llmConfigured()` (EITHER provider) at runtime → 503; pure LLM routes (`replies`/`drafter`/`voiceExtract`) refuse to mount unless `llmConfigured()`. `askLLM` still enforces the RESOLVED provider's key per request (503 `llm_not_configured`) — the mount/pre-flight gate is only "is ANY provider available". `images` stays `XAI_API_KEY`-only (Decision 6). The pre-flight 503 strings on pillars-draft/extract-winners/icebreaker stay `grok_not_configured` (stable extension matchers); only digest's degrade field renamed to `llm_not_configured`.
23. **Worker-owned statuses**: PATCH/DELETE 409 on `publishing`/`posted`. **A3.5:** `POST /posts/scheduled/:id/mark-posted` is the ONE sanctioned client status transition (`manual`→`posted`, 409 `not_manual` otherwise); it flips status only and NEVER writes `posts_published` (decision 6 — the discovery-checkpoint trap).
23a. **Advisory, never refusal** (GR.6 `scheduleWarnings` in `calendar.ts`): a "this looks risky" check ships as a `warnings: string[]` field computed AFTER the write, inside a try/catch, so a failed advisory read degrades to no advice instead of turning a 201 into a 500. Only money/policy guards (the URL surcharge) may refuse. Same family as "a side-hook failure never fails the paying path".

**Extension**
24. **Background = single session-storage writer**; content/panel talk via messages, never write directly.
25. **One transport**: all HTTP through `ApiRequest`; blobs via `ApiRequest.binary`.
26. **Content script is an IIFE**: no module imports at runtime; shared code gets inlined — heavy deps stay out.
27. **Shims for shared server modules** (replyBand [capture metadata only now], radarSweep, cannon, channelSuggest) — never fork logic between server and page. **RA.1 moved a live example across the line:** `bandStickiness` + the `RadarBandName` union left `extension/src/shared/radar.ts` for `src/shared/radarSweep.ts` the moment the SERVER started ratcheting bands too (the `radar_sightings` upsert), with `RadarBand` left behind as a type alias so no importer changed. The test is not "is it shared code" but **"do two sides now apply the same rule"** — `evictionWeight` stayed put by that test (cap pressure is a display rule the server never runs). Verify with `grep -rn "function bandStickiness" src extension` → exactly one hit.
- **A warn-and-drop client in front of an all-or-nothing route must mirror that route's per-field
  ceilings** (RA.2, `shared/radarIngest.ts`): `POST /x/radar/sightings` parses every row before writing
  any and 400s the whole batch on its first bad row (so a drifted reader is nameable), while the client
  drops a failed POST and never retries (so a lost sighting never costs a user action). Each half is
  right alone; together they mean **one unrepresentable row silently costs up to 99 good ones**. The
  mapper therefore returns `null` for a row the route would refuse — required field fails ⇒ drop the row,
  optional field fails ⇒ send `null`, because "unknown" is legal there — and restates the route's four
  ceilings (§7.33, the `CURATE_REQUEST_CAP`/`MAX_CURATE_TWEETS` precedent). Ask this of every new ingest
  pair: what does the server refuse, and who pays when the client can't hear the refusal?
28. **Posting is always manual paste** — OAuth 1.0a media wall + reply policy; nothing auto-posts to others, MCP can only create `draft` rows.
- **Design tokens (UI.8)**: the panel's `styles.css` `:root` carries the `--strat-*` token set (from `Stratus Design System/tokens/*.css`) + `--x-*` companion tokens + legacy short aliases. New UI references `--strat-*` directly; tinted fills use the exact fill tokens or `color-mix(in srgb, var(--strat-*) N%, transparent)`; **no color literal lives outside `:root`**. **UI.9** made it theme-aware: `:root[data-theme='light']` redefines only the base `--strat-*` tokens (the whole sheet re-tints via the aliases), `main.tsx` stamps `data-theme`/`data-density`/`data-scale` on `<html>` from the local `theme`/`density`/`uiScale` settings (`system` resolved via `matchMedia` + listener). Appearance is panel-local (chrome.storage), never server-synced; content-script overlays and the Studio canvas are exempt (they follow X / the brand kit). (Unnumbered — the numbered `§7.N` refs are load-bearing across CLAUDE.md/plans; don't renumber.)
- **Overlay tokens (UI.16)**: the on-page surfaces have their OWN palette — `OVERLAY_TOKENS`, a single `:root{}` block at the top of `content.ts` emitted ahead of every injected rule, exposing `--stratus-<tone>` + `-line` (1px outline) + `-fill` (tinted bg) for muted/blue/hot/warm/danger/pillar, `--stratus-muted-hairline` for structural dividers, and `--stratus-font`. **Never the panel's `--strat-*` here** (§7.26 — the sheet ships inside the IIFE and the overlay sits on X's theme, not the user's Appearance setting); a new chip family adds a tone to the block and references it, never a fresh literal. Same rule for the two public pages: `public/explorer.html` + `public/writer.html` each carry the DS palette written once with `light-dark()` (`color-scheme: light dark` follows the OS; a header button pins `data-theme` under the shared `explorer:theme` key) plus the short aliases their rules resolve through — the blocks are duplicated across the two files ON PURPOSE (no build step) and are edited together.
- **Settings platform (UI.1)**: server-side tunable knobs live in `app_settings` (override rows) + the typed `src/x/settings/registry.ts` catalog. Discipline: **only routes/workers read the store** via the bound `getSetting`; **pure modules stay pure** and take an opts object defaulted to today's constant (`computeQuests(rows, opts = QUEST_DEFAULTS)`) — so every existing pure test stays valid and the store is mockable. Registry floors/ceilings are the money/policy guard (an MCP agent editing via `x_update_setting` hits the same wall). The shared store (`src/settings/store.ts`) never imports `src/x/*` — the registry is passed in. **UI.2 landed the first store consumers:** `routes/brief.ts` reads `x.doctrine.anchors3/anchors4/ladderSwitchAt` (schedule gaps + ladder pick via `pickAnchors(n, cfg)`), `x.display.sparklineDays/leaderCount`, and `x.quests.*` (through `computeQuests(inputs, opts)` + the new trailing params on `neglectedTargetsAtDayStart`/`launchesAttended`) at request time. The reply band / week-% / 2–10× stay **niche-owned** (`loadDoctrine`, N.5) — D2/D30c dropped the 3 duplicate keys UI.1 had seeded, so each registry knob has exactly one owner. **UI.3 added the people/followups/pinned/digest consumers the same way:** `routes/followups.ts` reads the `followups` group per request (queue windows → `classifyFollowups`, momentum threshold → `momentumInflection`, reup ages → the SQL, fan-window → `fanUnacknowledged`); `routes/brief.ts` reads the `pinned` group → `buildPinnedWatch(…, {staleDays, outperformRatio})`; `routes/digest.ts` reads its own `x.digest.neglectedCap` PLUS the `followups` group's `neglectedTargetDays`/`neglectedAllyDays` (single owner, two consumers — the weekly list moves with the daily queue). One deliberate exception to "only routes/workers read the store": `people/store.ts::recomputePerson` reads the `people` group directly, because `computeStage` runs from every ingest path (mentions/harvest/engagements/PATCH) and a knob honored only in the route would leave the others on defaults — recomputePerson is impure DB access, not a pure fn. The 2–10× band multipliers were again NOT added as keys (niche-owned, the same D2 drop). **UI.4 added the gate/radar/worker consumers + the MCP pair:** `routes/playbook.ts` reads `x.gates.minCellN` as the DEFAULT gate (the `?minN=` query param still wins per read) and the guidance loaders read it too — a prompt is never steered by a thinner bar than the page shows; `routes/metrics.ts` and `routes/brief.ts` both read `x.gates.bestTimeMinN` (one owner, two consumers — the best-times list and the Today cadence gaps gate identically, `annotateGaps(…, minN)` being the pure param); `routes/radar.ts` reads `x.radar.draftTtlH` for its lazy expiry; ~~`workers/dailyMetrics.ts` reads the winner-re-read floor/cap at the start of each run~~ (**XD.1: worker deleted; `x.workers.winnerRereadMinViews`/`…Cap`/`dailyMetricsHourUtc`/`discoveryExcludeReplies` deleted with it. The view floor survived as `x.followups.reupMinViews` — same number, same `WINNER_REREAD_MIN_VIEWS` env seed, but its only reader is now the $0 re-up-candidate SELECT in `routes/followups.ts`; an override row under the old key is orphaned, not migrated**); `index.ts::startXWorkers` reads the ONE remaining cadence knob (`x.workers.publisherIntervalSec`, `appliesOn:'restart'`, decision 10). MCP `x_settings` (curated) + `x_update_setting` (write) go through the same routes, so registry ceilings hold for an agent. **UI.5 added the MONEY groups (`budgets`/`ai`/`mentions`) — 13 groups, 41 knobs — under one extra rule: a money knob is read at REQUEST time inside the refuse-before-spend ladder, never captured earlier.** `costTracker` takes `dailyBudgetUsd` as a number OR a getter (X passes one over `x.budgets.xSoftDailyUsd`), resolved per cost event and per `/cost` read; `images.ts` reads `x.budgets.imageDailyUsd` per call and `0` genuinely disables generation; ~~`routes/mentions.ts` reads the refresh cap + page size before the token fetch~~ (**XD.1: the whole `mentions` group — `serverRefreshCap`/`panelRefreshCap`/`pullMax` — is deleted with `POST /mentions/refresh`. Registry was 61 knobs / 15 groups / 31 mirrored at that point; SW.1 and OU.3 have since taken it to **69 / 16 / 33** — see the `settings/registry.ts` row in §3.3 for the live total**). The `x.ai.*` knobs are the **house-default tier `askLLM` merges last** (request body > the `ai` blob from Settings → AI > these) — they tune the tier the blob's `null` fields already defer to, so the AI.2 settings and the registry are not two owners of one number. Threading rule for a knob whose call site also carries a caller-intent flag: give it its OWN opt (`pullMentions({pullMax})` beside `maxResults`) rather than reusing the flag — reusing it here would have re-broken CA.1's 800-cap walk. **UI.6 extended the discipline across the wire (the mirror):** a `scope:'mirrored'` knob rides to the extension in one background-fetched blob, and the panel repeats the server's split — pure modules take a trailing defaulted `cfg`, only COMPONENTS read the blob (via `useServerSettings()`), and the baked fallbacks have exactly one owner (`extension/src/shared/serverSettings.ts`). Two rules that fall out of it: **(a)** the fallback is per key, not per blob — one corrupt value must not drop the others back to baked; **(b)** a knob is only mirrored if the client genuinely acts on it, and never when a server-side backstop is the real limit (`serverRefreshCap` stays server-only while `panelRefreshCap` mirrors). Full wiring in §5's mirrored-settings paragraph. **UI.7 closed the loop with the first knob BOTH sides act on** (`x.band.*`, 14 groups / 53 knobs): the server gate in `routes/replies.ts` and the on-page badge in `content.ts` classify through the same `classifyBand(signals, thresholds)`, one reading `settings/bandThresholds.ts`, the other the mirrored blob. Three rules it adds: **(a) when a knob's owner is a shared pure module, the registry defaults ARE that module's constant** (`BAND`) and a test asserts the group is exactly the module's shape — a partially-exposed rule is worse than an unexposed one, because the half a user can't reach looks like a bug; **(b)** a hoisted literal is a knob like any other, so hoisting one means hoisting the whole rule it belongs to; **(c)** a measurement surface takes the configured thresholds only when it describes a LIVE surface — `buildTimelineFunnel` (the opportunity funnel over what the badge highlighted) does, `scoreReplyOutcome`'s fallback (the band CROSSTAB, the evidence a recalibration is judged on, mostly capture-time stamps) deliberately does not. **UI.12 added the fourth mirror reason and the PANEL-side discipline (14 groups / 57 knobs, 23 mirrored):** a knob whose only consumer is the side panel must be `mirrored` or it is unreachable by the code that reads it — that is the four `x.display.*` Today caps. And when a panel constant duplicates a number the server already owns, **flip the server key to mirrored rather than mint a display twin** (`x.followups.neglectedTargetDays` — the Today roster tint, the Do-next queue and the Sunday digest are now one number; `x.ai.batchReplyCap` — mirrored purely so `radarBatchSize()` can clamp the display cap to the batch size the server will actually accept, since an oversized batch is REFUSED, not truncated). The panel mirror of "one place edits a knob" is `sidepanel/settingsEditor.ts::useSettingsEditor` — optimistic → 400 ms debounce per key → flush on unmount → re-read on refusal — with **one editor per tab**, shared by every `SettingsGear` on it; two editors mean two registry copies and a gear edit that leaves Tuning stale. An inline gear whose keys are missing renders nothing at all. (Unnumbered — see the `don't renumber` note above.)
- **UI primitives (UI.10, D7 standing)**: every NEW panel surface from Wave 1 on composes `src/sidepanel/ui/` primitives (Section/EmptyState/SubTabs/SettingRow/Slider/GearPopover) + `--strat-*` tokens — no bespoke `<h3>`/muted-`<p>`/hand-rolled controls. Primitives are pure presentation (className + tokens, no state libs, no API calls); the settings PATCH lives in `settingsClient.ts`, and the panel renders knobs from `GET /x/settings` (extension never imports the server registry). Wave-5 polish (UI.12–16) migrates the pre-masterplan tabs onto them. (Unnumbered — see the `don't renumber` note above.) **UI.11 (the first full consumer) adds the write discipline for any registry-editing surface:** render from `GET /x/settings` and never from the server registry (§5 build isolation); hold the edit OPTIMISTICALLY and **debounce the PATCH ~400 ms per key** (a `Slider` fires on every drag tick — one PATCH per tick is a write storm), recomputing `isDefault` locally so the reset dot tracks; **flush the debounce on unmount**, because switching subtab would otherwise silently drop a knob the user already moved; and on a server refusal show the 400 code on the row and **re-read the whole response** — the registry floors/ceilings are the money guard (§8), so a value the server rejected must never sit on screen looking saved. **UI.15 added the rule for a `server`-scoped knob edited inline:** a mirrored knob takes effect on the next render, but a server knob shapes the RESPONSE (the Playbook's every `sufficient` flag is computed at `minN`), so the surface has to **re-read itself** after the editor's debounce lands — once per distinct value, guarded by a ref holding the value already re-read for, because a value the registry bounds refuse would otherwise poll forever (the editor re-reads on refusal, which settles it the other way). Only do this on a $0 route that writes nothing — four reads in this repo WRITE and may never be polled (§7 read-that-writes). **UI.12 made that discipline a module** (`sidepanel/settingsEditor.ts::useSettingsEditor`) rather than a pattern to re-type, and added the rules an INLINE gear needs: **one editor per tab, handed to every gear** (a per-gear editor holds its own registry copy, so an edit in one goes stale in the others); `resetKey` **cancels** a pending debounce rather than flushing it (dropping the override is the newer intent); a gear renders `null` when its keys aren't there, because an empty popover reads as a broken feature while the section itself keeps working off the mirrored blob; and a gear's `note` carries the OWNERSHIP line for whatever number a user will look for in it and not find (UI.11's `GROUP_NOTE`, moved next to the feature). **UI.13 (the first `numberArray` gear, and the first gear inside a `<form>`) added two primitive-level rules:** a control that commits on BLUR cannot be left to an outside click — closing the popover unmounts it, and removing a focused input does NOT fire `blur`, so `GearPopover`'s outside-click handler blurs the focused descendant BEFORE `setOpen(false)`; and any text-ish control in a gear must swallow **Enter** (`preventDefault` + commit), because a gear next to a feature is often inside that feature's form, where Enter is "submit". Both fixes live in the primitives, not the tab — the next gear inherits them. Also: two tabs may share ONE key list (`composerLogic.CADENCE_SETTING_KEYS`) when they render the same underlying numbers; the per-tab part is the `note`, not the keys.
- **Chip taxonomy (UI.14, extended UI.15)**: ONE chip shape (`.chip`, aliased by `.stage-chip`/`.people-angle-chip`/`.reply-variant`) plus five tone modifiers (`.chip-{ok,accent,warn,strong,muted}`), and each vocabulary maps its values onto a tone in `sidepanel/chips.ts` — never a new class with its own padding and radius. Absorbed `.stage-chip`, `.people-angle-chip` and `.dm-status`, which were three geometries of the same object. **Deliberately outside the family:** the scheduled-post ramp `.badge-*` (a pipeline state, uppercase and denser), `.radar-band-*` (a classifier verdict the on-page badge mirrors in the separate `--stratus-*` palette, D137c) the GR.8 goal-pacing chip, and **SC.4's `.coach-chip`** (it sits INSIDE a `.chip`, and a chip within a chip reads as two labels — it borrows the three `.coach-tone-*` colours and takes its border from `currentColor`) — different alphabets, and the GR.8 comment in `styles.css` says why collapsing them misleads. Tones are alias tokens, so both themes come free. **Renaming a shared class is a cross-lane edit**: `.stage-chip` is rendered by five files, three of them in UI.15's lane, which is why the base was ALIASED rather than renamed — and UI.15 hit the identical wall from the other side (`.reply-variant` is rendered by `Conversations.tsx`, a UI.12 file), so it aliased too. The general rule: **a class rendered outside your lane is not yours to rename, however mechanical the diff** — add the base to the selector list and let the old tone alias survive. A new vocabulary is a lookup in `chips.ts`, never a sixth family: UI.15 added `replyDraftChip` that way. **Dead-class audits give false zeros here** — `.badge-draft`/`-pending`/`-posted`/`-cancelled` have ZERO literal occurrences in the tree and are all live, built by `` `badge badge-${r.status}` `` in `Calendar.tsx`/`Today.tsx`; grep for `` `badge-${ `` and `chip chip-${` before deleting anything.

**Process**
29. **Docs sync in the same commit**: `docs/PHASE-HISTORY.md` phase entry (NOT CLAUDE.md — slimmed 2026-07-23; CLAUDE.md changes only when a guardrail changes), the relevant plan doc (PLAN/CIRCLES/SURFACES), the matching `docs/<tab>.md`, and THIS codemap.
30. **Smoke script per feature**: rerunnable, $0 default, `--live` for the one paid verification, cleans up after itself.
31. **No obvious comments; comments explain why** (cost trade-off, policy quirk, race). No emojis.
32. **Never write a raw control char into source — use the escape** (RL.7): `src/x/playbook.ts` held two literal NUL bytes as a composite-key sentinel, which made `file` report it as `data` and made **every `grep` over it silently return nothing** (`grep -a` was the only way to find `classifyReplyOrigin`). Fixed to `'\0'`; identical at runtime, greppable again. One-command audit: `for f in $(git ls-files '*.ts'); do file $f | grep -q ': data' && echo $f; done`.
33. **A ported threshold is validated against OUR corpus before it ships** (SC.6, and SC decision 1 states it as doctrine — "a number is a measurement or it is absent"). x-builder's cooldown clusters a window by token-set Jaccard **≥0.45**; measured over stratus's own 137 published originals the most similar same-format pair inside any 7-day window scores **0.238** (p95 0.077, median token set 15 words), so the guard would have shipped permanently inert and nobody would have noticed — a silent feature looks identical to a working one. The recipe is the SC.2/SC.5 one and costs nothing: pull `GET /x/data/posts_published?limit=200&offset=N` from prod with the `.env` bearer (S1 explorer, $0) and run the new pure function locally, including a **rolling-window replay** when the thing being shipped is a counter (it prints the lit-rate per bucket, which is the only way to tell "warns usefully" from "warns always"). Do this BEFORE the thresholds reach a test file — a fixture proves the arithmetic, never the calibration.
34. **Validate the borrowed METHOD, not just the borrowed number** (SC.8, generalizing rule 33 one level up). SC.8's plan named two house readers to copy — `latestOutcomes`' latest-snapshot-wins and `buildBestTimes`' `views*1440/age` normalization. Both are correct where they live and both are wrong as the numerator of a cross-post ratio: the latest snapshot only differs from the first on posts that were **re-read because they won**, so it is two measurement protocols selected on the outcome; and the linear age model is falsified by our own data (posts read at <12h and at 12–27h carry the same raw views, so dividing by age manufactures a 2.7× spread and one 4-minute read became a 696× multiplier). **"Latest row wins" is right for displaying one row and wrong for comparing many whenever the re-read is selective** — check which, and check any normalization against the data it will be applied to, before it reaches a test file. The $0 way is the S1 explorer: `POST /x/data/query` with the first-vs-latest snapshot both pulled, then run the candidate fit locally (`scratchpad`, not committed). **XR.3 addendum — a borrowed method can carry a filter that cannot be satisfied, and the check is to run it against the corpus it was borrowed FROM.** The XR plan asked for a 48h maturity cut on the feed sample; measured, **zero** of our 766 passive-timeline rows are 48h old at capture (max 44.6h — a Home Timeline shows recent posts, so the corpus structurally cannot hold a settled reading), and **zero of Bangermeter's own 141-post reference sample are either** (median 6h, max 43h, read off its `ageMin` column; `calibration/calibrate.js` filters only on `views > 0` and never reads it). The cut would have emptied the corpus it came from. Clocked the other way — against the sample's newest post — it is a collection-recency filter, not a maturity filter, and moves the medians <8%. Shipped as a **reported diagnostic**: the reference must be sampled like the thing it scores (every post E scores is a feed-time DOM reading too), and rerun stability comes from clocking against `captured_at`, which is frozen per row. **`scripts/calibrate-ranker.ts` is the reusable recipe** for the whole shape — pull the corpus with `POST /x/data/query`, seed a scratchpad SQLite from it, and run the REAL script against it so the constants come from the deliverable rather than from a second implementation in SQL.
35. **A parser over a PAID response is asymmetric on purpose — decide per field which half it is in** (JD.3; `judge/prompt.ts::parseVerdict` is the exemplar, `parseRewrite`/`parseDm`/`parseIcebreakers` are the same shape stated less explicitly). Returning `null` costs the caller the money already spent, so the strict half must be small and load-bearing: for the judge it is the thirteen scores (a missing dimension renders as a hole the panel cannot explain, so `null` is right), and everything else degrades — a missing headline reads as `''`, an unusable annotation is dropped while its neighbours survive, over-long one-liners are clipped, an unknown enum becomes `null` rather than a guess. **Two rules that fall out of it and that a later reader will otherwise re-litigate:** an *explicit* `null` from the model is a stated unknown (§7.11) while an *absent* key is a malformed shape — `audienceMatch: null` parses, `audienceMatch` missing does not; and a range/cap the schema cannot express (`minimum`/`maximum`/`minItems` are on the strict-structured-outputs unsupported list, the threadPrompt/RU.3/AI.8 rejection risk) is enforced **here**, which is why the parser and not the schema is what a test pins. **ML.2 is the second exemplar, and it is the cleaner one to point an implementer at because the split is one field wide:** `parseReplyVariants`/`parseBatchReplies` keep `text` and `angle` strict — a bad one poisons what you paste — while **`gloss` is lenient**: missing, `null`, non-string or blank all become `null` and **the variant survives**, and an over-long gloss is clipped at `MAX_GLOSS_LENGTH` (400) rather than rejected. The asymmetry is the whole decision: the gloss is a reading aid on a variant you have ALREADY paid for, so refusing it would trade a convenience for the entire response. It also carries the schema-shape corollary the judge only implies: strict json_schema has **no optional properties**, so a field that may legitimately be absent ships as `{type:['string','null']}` **AND in `required`** — nullable-and-required is the only shape the provider accepts, and the leniency then lives in the parser rather than the schema. And the third: **a product rule is not a parser rule.** The non-English path wants exactly one variant, and `maxItems` is unavailable (D164b) — but the trim lives in the ROUTE (`trimToSingleVariant`, §3.3), because a parser that silently drops paid variants is the wrong place for it. The parser answers "is this shape usable"; the route answers "how many of these do we want".
36. **A comparison between two model outputs is only meaningful if the grader is PINNED** (JD.5; `routes/judge.ts::/judge/apply`). The never-worse guard is `rewriteOverall > originalOverall` — two numbers that mean nothing unless the same rubric, the same server-stamped grounding, the same schema, the same temperature AND the same model/provider produced both. So the re-judge runs through the shared `judgeOnce` helper rather than a second hand-written call site, and it is pinned to the **stored** judgment's `model`+`provider`, not to the caller's override (which steers only the writer). Generalizes past this route: **any "is B better than A" check across two LLM calls owns the grader as part of its contract** — a per-call provider override at the top of the precedence chain (which `askLLM` has, decision 11) is exactly the knob that silently turns such a guard into a coin flip. Corollary from the same task: pick the direction of the tie deliberately and pin it with a test. At a near-deterministic temperature a cosmetic rewrite TIES far more often than it loses, so `>=` would hand back a machine's rephrasing on no evidence; `>` is why the guard is a guard.

**RC reply-craft pattern addendum (binds existing §7.4/§7.11/§7.14/§7.16/§7.19/§7.33; no renumbering):**

- **Refuse-before-spend includes free resolution order.** Reply mode is `$0` SQL + pure detection, but the single route still runs it after the band gate. §7.4 is about order, not amount. The old specificity heuristic has a vote only for `personaUse:'full'`; applying its builder-noun regex to any other room yields unknown, not fail, so no paid regeneration and no primary reordering there.
- **`null`/fallback provenance stays visible.** `detectReplyMode` and an unrecognized explicit/curated/roster string return no mode and fall through; only the resolver maps the final miss to `general` with `source:'fallback'`. Outcome attribution cannot claim that fallback was a measured general-room verdict, so `ownReplyMode` reports `unknown` instead. Same distinction, two consumers.
- **One resolver, two routes, per-post semantics.** `resolveReplyMode` is called over one target for Reply Master and N targets for Radar; no call site reimplements precedence. This is intentionally asymmetric with language: language is set-wide because one tail clause controls the call, mode rides inside every rendered POST because a mixed queue is expected. Server echo is the only UI source — never re-detect client-side.
- **Cacheable instruction vs rendered value is an architectural split.** Persona scope/humanization/length/opening rules are constant and therefore a three-file byte-sync edit in the head. Mode, its angle/register/budget/move, and measured winners vary by post and therefore append at the tail. Moving either half across that boundary changes prefix-cache cost and requires an explicit reason.
- **Strict schema optimization, route product rule.** Narrow the angle enum so the provider cannot invent a forbidden label and does not pay for obvious wrong-room variants; still trim after parse because strict structured output cannot use `maxItems`. On a mixed batch the schema gets the union and the route trims per post. If trimming would discard every paid variant, preserve the payload and degrade the label — paid text is more valuable than an empty answer (§7.35).
- **Two calibration clocks.** Comparative Playbook cells stay n≥20; room budgets/moves recalibrate only at ≥30 replies in that room. `ANGLE_VOCABULARY_WIDENED_AT` is a hard date boundary, not UI decoration: pre-date `extends` contains unrepresentable observation/question shapes. Opening analysis always reports capture basis points beside raw yield, because the baseline's raw lead was entirely parent-size confounding. A borrowed opening rule is a guess until this within-room table can retire it (§7.33).
