**XR.4 addendum to rule 34 — check a borrowed threshold at BOTH ends, and check whether one set of cuts is serving two distributions.** D230 predicted `RANKER_BAND_CUTS`'s upper cut was wrong and it was; the measurement found the *lower* one deader (`below` fired on 0.3% of our own published originals against `strong`'s 31%). It also found the real defect underneath: `rankerBand` was one function over two scales whose distributions differ by an order of magnitude in spread, so no single pair could ever centre both — moving the cuts to fit C would have made E almost entirely `below`. Two symptoms worth naming, because they are cheap to look for: **a band that fires on ~0% or ~100% of a real corpus is a dead instrument reading as a working one**, and **a threshold with two callers is two thresholds until proven otherwise.** The fix pattern is the one this repo already uses for direction flags — two named functions, nothing to pass — plus a `*_SAMPLE` stamp that pins the RULE (cuts = the corpus's q1/q3) so the next recalibration must move the cuts and their provenance together.

**RA.6 addendum — a smoke script reads JSON, so nothing type-checks its field names.** `smoke-passive-harvest.ts` asserted `cell.band === 'unknown'` on the timeline funnel; `db96a4c` (2026-08-11) renamed `FunnelCell.band` → `bucket` and the script went red on its last step and **stayed red for a week** — no `bun test`, typecheck or lint covers `scripts/`'s *response* shapes, because the body is cast from `await res.json()`. Two rules: **(1)** renaming a field on any response a smoke reads is a two-file change, exactly like the doc count strings; `grep -rn '<oldField>' scripts/` before you land the rename. **(2)** A red smoke is evidence about the SCRIPT until you've located the assertion — here the route, the transport and the data were all fine and only the reader's vocabulary had moved.

## 8. Cost & policy invariants (condensed — full text in CLAUDE.md)

- URL in post text = **$0.20 vs $0.015** (13x). `createPost` guard; links go in first reply ($0.030 total). **Manual-publish exemption (A3.5, decision 5):** the calendar's URL guard is `pending`-only — a `manual` post is pasted by hand (no API call), so it may hold a link freely; manual mode IS the sanctioned $0 link-post path. Articles likewise never hit the API, so the surcharge never applies to them.
- **Feb 2026**: programmatic replies to non-self tweets blocked on self-serve (except when @-mentioned — unverified, `MENTION_API_REPLIES=false`). Quote-of-others blocked. Self-reply/self-quote OK (self-quote verified via `verifiedSelfQuote`).
- Token rotation: persist new refresh token BEFORE returning access token.
- **The only billed X call is `createPost` (invariant #8, 2026-08-12).** Every read — the 03:00 daily pass, `POST /posts/reconcile`, `POST /posts/backfill`, `POST /mentions/refresh`, and the `getTweet`/`searchRecent`/`getUserTweets`/`getUserMentions`/`getTweetsByIds` functions — was deleted. `src/app.test.ts::no billed read routes exist` keeps those POSTs 404. Price table below is for reading historical `cost_events` rows and for the day someone argues a read back in: owned reads $0.001; other-user reads $0.005; third-party user lookup $0.010; post $0.015; delete $0.010.
- Media upload requires OAuth 1.0a — **not supported**; Studio images are manual paste.
- Budgets: X soft $0.15/day (log), xAI images hard $0.50/day (429). **UI.5: both AMOUNTS are settings** (`x.budgets.xSoftDailyUsd` ≤ $1, `x.budgets.imageDailyUsd` ≤ $2, env vars seed the defaults) read per call; the CHECKS are never settings (Decision 5) — soft always logs, the image gate always refuses, and `imageDailyUsd: 0` means "no image generation", not "use the default".
- Out of scope v1: multi-tenant, follower sync, media upload, Chrome Web Store, idempotency drafts, per-tier caps.

(d) `POST /searches/compile` answers **200 with `problems` + `url: null`** and stores no row — the panel compiles locally through the shim, so this script is that route's only caller. (e) **The capture footer writer-to-reader (D220)** — `POST /voice/scrape` with `sourcePath: '/search?q=…'` moves `capture.savedFromSearch` **+1**, a `/home` one **+0**, and the `voice_tweets.source` column is then read directly: the provenance string is two literals in two files (`routes/voice.ts::SOURCE_OUTLIER`, `routes/searches.ts::CAPTURE_SOURCE`) and a typo in either leaves the footer at 0 forever while both files' own unit tests stay green. (f) DELETE → 204, then 404 on the re-read AND the re-delete. Cleanup runs on entry as well as from `fail()` and the success path: `__smoke_outliers__`-prefixed rows, the `9008xxx` tweets plus their `voice_authors`/`people`/`person_events` side-hook rows, and every `x.outliers.*` knob snapshot-restored by `isDefault` (never `reset`, which would delete a real override).
- `calibrate-ranker.ts` (**XR.3**) — **not a smoke; the smoke count stays 41** (XR.8 owns 42). Read-only `SELECT` over `harvest_rows mode='timeline'`, deduped at `min(captured_at)` like `loadTimelineFunnel`, `views > 0`, and it derives `X_OBSERVED_RATES` as **per-post medians** using `calibrate.js`'s own quantile (`sort asc, index min(len-1, floor(p*len))`) rather than the repo's `median()` — the borrowed method is the thing under test. **Refuses to emit constants below n=100** and prints `n` either way. Three things it prints that a rerun depends on: the **age-at-capture distribution** (reported, never cut — rule 34's addendum), the **before/after E-score distribution over the same corpus** (the swap took our feed's median reading from **63 with 77% above 50** to **50 with 43%**, which is the whole §7.33 argument), and a **helper check** proving its rate-parameterised scorer reproduces `scoreMeasured` on every row — without that the counterfactual column is a fiction (D184a). It also names the finding it cannot fix: K=2000 was borrowed from a feed whose median post has 6,600 views, ours has 297, so a typical reading is pulled ~87% onto the reference and E's p10..p90 spans only 32..54. **XR.4 paid that off and the answer inverted the suspicion — K stays at 2000 (MoM ~1066 on `favorite`, no between-post signal at all on `reply`/`retweet`), and what was actually broken was the band cut.** So the script now derives TWO things in one $0 pass: the rates above, and **`RANKER_BAND_CUTS`** — C over `posts_published` originals (no lexicon on purpose: two coach checks move with it, and a constant that changes when the niche is re-pinned is not a constant; measured, the quartiles are identical either way) and E over `harvest_rows mode != 'replies'` deduped at first sighting, each printing shipped-vs-measured band shares and a paste block, each refusing below n=100. Verified end-to-end against a scratch DB seeded from prod: it re-emits `56/68` and `46/51` exactly.
- Studio (S5) browser verification (ST.9, 2026-07-18): the deterministic-render discipline (S3) — a throwaway Bun-served harness bundles the real `compose`/`templates`/`registry` modules and renders every template onto a canvas in Chrome; confirms fonts/mascot/presets/pattern-determinism/Copy-PNG. Reusable pattern for future Studio visual QA; the harness entry is not committed.
- Gates before commit: `bun test` + `bun run typecheck` + `bun run lint`.
- Deploy: `./scripts/deploy.sh` (rsync, migrate — aborts restart on failure, `.git-sha` stamp, `curl -f /healthz`).

## 10. Recipes — where new things go

- **New API surface**: pure logic in `src/x/<domain>.ts` or `src/x/<domain>/` → router in `src/x/routes/<name>.ts` → mount in `src/x/index.ts` (mind order + Grok gating) → route test + pure test → smoke script → docs sync. If MCP-worthy, add a curated tool in `src/x/mcp.ts` (in-process `app.request`) — that bumps `src/mcp.test.ts`'s **exact** asserted tool count (now **28**) AND `docs/s2-mcp-server.md`'s **six** unasserted strings in the SAME commit: the prose total, the `## The tools` heading, the end-to-end verification line, the `### <tier> (N)` heading **of the tier you touched**, the intro's prose enumeration of the write tools, and the §"Security & cost invariants" row naming the write ceiling. `scripts/smoke-mcp.ts`'s expected-names list and the counts in §3.3's `mcp.ts` row + §6 here go with them.
- **New table/column**: `src/x/db/schema.ts` → `bun run db:generate` → inspect SQL for dropped seeds → consumers. Column semantics: nullable + null=unknown when backfill is impossible.
- **New worker**: `src/x/workers/` → register heartbeat + stop() in `startXWorkers` → healthz staleness window. Prefer read-time computation over a new worker when $0-equivalent (§7.12).
- **New extension surface**: component in `src/sidepanel/` → wire in `App.tsx` → API via `api.ts` → shared pure logic in `src/shared/` or `extension/src/shared/` (bun-tested) → `docs/<tab>-tab.md`. Content-script additions must stay IIFE-safe.
- **New prompt-affecting feature**: NEVER edit the template mid-file — inject at the variable tail; keep byte-sync tests green; stamp what the model saw into the draft's snapshot.
- **New measurement**: pure `build*` in `src/x/playbook.ts` (gated) → loader in `routes/playbook.ts` → Playbook tab section → optionally digest facts.

Reported right after UI.18 shipped: a canned pick landed in the reply box as several hundred characters of `gogogogd…` for a 45-char line. **Cause (not UI.18):** X's composer applies its own model update on `beforeinput` **and** lets the browser apply the native one, so every synthetic keystroke of the 18ms-per-char `execCommand('insertText')` loop went in twice and the duplication compounded. Modes `inserted|copied|failed` → `DELIVER_HINT`. Removed: `typeTextInto`, `insertChar`, `TYPE_CHAR_DELAY_MS`, `cancelTyping` + its Escape branch (a fill is atomic, there is nothing to abort); `clearReplyEditor` now selects with a Range (`selectAllIn`) instead of `execCommand('selectAll')`. Cmd+B fills instead of typing. Settings copy "Auto-type"→"Auto-fill" (`Settings.tsx`, `storage.ts`, `docs/settings-tab.md`, `docs/replies-tab.md`). **Verified** in a scratch harness across four editor shapes — plain contenteditable, textarea, a paste-handling Lexical-ish editor, and a `beforeinput` double-applier reproducing the X bug — all four filled exactly once (paste path for the paste-handler, insertText for the rest). Gates: `bun test` 1567/0, root+extension typecheck, lint, extension build all green. Live x.com walk is still the user's ship check (§8).
